island: Minjerribah / North Stradbroke Island, Quandamooka Country, Queensland, Australia
about: The grammar of the micro drama series. Not scripts. This pack holds the parts a director system assembles into stories that the simulation is already telling: what conditions open a thread, who gets cast, which beats need which state change, where a choice actually forks, and how a thread can end well, badly or quietly. The island writes the plot. This file only teaches the director how to notice.
honesty: No seed here is a record of something that happened to a real person on this island. Every seed is a situation type built from public conditions: a timetable, a swell forecast, a council lever, a species record, a census number. The specific people are generated.
Where a seed rests on a mechanism, the mechanism carries a source. Where it rests on a plausible island pattern, it says so and carries low confidence.

The state paths in the triggers are a contract with systems that mostly do not exist yet. Every path is listed in state_contract with an exists flag against src/systems/manifest.js. A director must read defensively and skip any seed whose paths are missing.
There is no dialogue in this pack, on purpose. Beats describe what happens and what changes, never what anyone says. See tone_guide.no_speech.

Several seeds turn on numbers nobody has published: how many houses at Amity are affected, how often the barge is actually cancelled, how many people leave the island in a year. Those seeds fire on relative movement, not on an invented absolute.
Endings are not scored. A thread that ends quietly is not a failure state. Most things on an island end quietly.

Seven of the businesses referenced in refs blocks carry status trading-unconfirmed in data/businesses.json: Stradbroke Cab Service, Straddie Mobile Vet, Cellarbrations Dunwich, Point Lookout Bushcare, Friends of Stradbroke Island, the North Stradbroke Island Aboriginal and Islander Housing Society, and Nareeba Moopi Moopi Pa. They are listed as candidate places and actors, not as guaranteed ones. The director checks status at runtime and substitutes or skips. See director.hard_rules.
No seed references a business whose status is closed or proposed. Sandy Sports Club, Rufus King Seafoods and the Amity Point Progress Association appear nowhere in this pack.

confidence_scale.high: The mechanism is documented in a citable public source or in another pack in this repo that cites one.
confidence_scale.medium: The mechanism follows from something documented, but the specific shape is a modelling choice.
confidence_scale.low: Plausible island pattern. Nobody has published this. Do not present it as fact and expect a local to correct it.

tone_guide.summary: Understated. Dry. Things happen, people cope, the tide keeps going. The drama is in what is not said and in who turns up.
do: Write flat declaratives. The event carries the weight; the sentence does not have to.
Prefer the concrete noun to the adjective. A boat, a bin, a fence post, a road. Not "a stunning coastline".
Let competence be interesting. Someone who knows exactly what to do in a bad hour is more watchable than someone falling apart.
Use the island's own units: a barge sailing, a tide, a school term, a long weekend, a season of whales.
Let humour be dry and sideways, and let it come from people knowing each other too well.
Allow anticlimax. The wind drops. The thing does not happen. That is an ending.
Name the real place, the real road, the real business, or name nothing.
do_not: No melodrama. Nobody screams, nobody has an epiphany, nobody gives a speech.
No tourist brochure language. Never "pristine", "paradise", "hidden gem", "untouched", "breathtaking", "idyllic", "escape".
No overstatement. Not "the worst storm in living memory". A storm is enough.
No moralising. The pack does not tell the player who was right.
No villains. The developer, the council officer, the holiday owner and the greenie all have a reason.
No trauma as texture. Poverty, illness, family violence and death are not set dressing. If a seed touches them, it is the subject and it is handled plainly.
No em dashes. Colon, semicolon, comma or full stop.
No invented Quandamooka words, no invented ceremony, no invented place names, no invented businesses, no invented roads.

no_speech.rule: The director never generates quoted speech for any character, and the chronicle never attributes words to anyone.
no_speech.why: Two reasons, and both matter. First, generated dialogue is where a place stops sounding like itself. Second, this is Quandamooka Country and roughly a quarter of the resident population is Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander. Putting generated words in a Quandamooka mouth is not acceptable, and a rule that applies to one group only is a worse rule than a rule that applies to everyone. So nobody speaks. People act, and the chronicle reports the action.
allowed_instead: Who turned up and who did not.
What changed in a number the player can see.

chronicle_style.length: One sentence per beat. Two at the absolute most.
chronicle_style.person: Third person, past tense, no narrator opinion.
chronicle_style.naming: Use the generated agent name and the real place name. Never a nickname the player has not seen.
chronicle_style.example_good: The 15:30 barge did not run, and by six there were eleven cars still on the apron at Toondah.
chronicle_style.example_bad: Chaos erupted at the ferry terminal as devastated families faced an agonising wait.

beat_grammar.summary: Five stages. Not every thread uses all five, and the order is fixed when they appear. A thread that stops after complication is a thread that went nowhere, which is allowed and is sometimes the point.

stages.one_line: A normal thing, established as normal before it breaks.
stages.rule: The setup beat must show the world working. It fires on ordinary state, not on the trigger. If the director cannot show the ordinary version first, it delays the thread rather than opening cold.
stages.legibility: The player should be able to say what this household normally does on a Tuesday.

stages.one_line: The island does something. Nobody chose it.
stages.rule: The complication is always driven by simulated state, never by narrative fiat. If the swell did not come up, the Gorge does not close. The director may wait for state; it may not create it.
stages.legibility: The cause must be visible somewhere in the UI at the moment it fires: a swell number, a cancelled sailing, a stock level, a road strike count.

stages.one_line: Someone has to decide, and both options cost something.
stages.rule: A choice beat is only a choice if each option changes state differently and none of them is free. If one option strictly dominates, it is not a choice beat, it is a consequence beat with extra steps. Some choices belong to the player, some to a resident, and some to nobody at all.
stages.legibility: The player can see the two costs before the fork resolves, whether or not the choice is theirs.

stages.one_line: What that cost, paid by someone.
stages.rule: Consequence must move at least one number the player can find, and at least one relationship. If neither moved, the beat did not happen.
stages.legibility: Second order is where the depth is: the cancelled barge is beat three, the cook who lost a shift is beat four.

stages.one_line: The island goes back to normal, slightly changed.
stages.rule: The coda writes the relationship change and closes the thread. It never resolves the underlying problem, because the underlying problems here are structural: erosion, the crossing, the housing, the season. The coda is about the people.
stages.legibility: One line in the chronicle and one changed relationship the player can inspect later.

beat_grammar.ordering_rule: setup then complication then choice then consequence then coda. A stage may be skipped. A stage may not be repeated inside one thread, except complication, which may fire twice at most when the island genuinely does the thing twice.
beat_grammar.silence_rule: A beat does not have to fire on the day it becomes eligible. The director may hold a beat for up to its seed patience_days, and should, because things landing on consecutive days reads as a script.

registers.label: Wry
registers.note: Something has gone wrong in a way that is mostly funny. Nobody is hurt. Used for logistics failures.

registers.label: Quiet worry
registers.note: A thing that might get worse. Handled by getting on with the day. Used for erosion, water, money.

registers.label: Slow grief
registers.note: A loss that is not sudden and cannot be fought. Used for leaving, for a place changing, for an animal that does not make it. Never more than two of these open at once.

registers.label: Steady competence
registers.note: People who know what to do, doing it. Volunteers, skippers, rangers, nurses. The most under-used register in games and the best one here.

registers.label: Neighbourly friction
registers.note: Two people who will still see each other on Thursday. Nothing is resolved and nothing is broken.

registers.label: Small relief
registers.note: The thing did not happen, or it happened and was survivable. Short threads.

registers.label: Civic friction
registers.note: The argument is real, both sides are reasonable, and the decision belongs to somebody who is not in the room.

registers.label: Held breath
registers.note: An outcome pending on something nobody controls: weather, a boat, a diagnosis. Resolves either way.

registers.label: Homecoming
registers.note: Someone returns, and it is more complicated than they expected. Rare. At most one at a time.

registers.label: Plain good
registers.note: A good day, honestly reported, no irony. The island needs these or the whole thing reads as decline.

cast_model.principle: Cast by archetype, never by name. The director draws a household from data/residents.json household_archetypes that matches the role, then draws the individual from that household. If no household matches and is available, the seed does not run.
cast_model.naming: Names come from residents.json name_pools and the pool policy. Never name an agent after a real islander, and never give an agent a real person's role at a real organisation.
cast_model.availability: A household is available if it is not the primary cast of an active thread and is off its post-thread cooldown. Supporting roles may be shared across threads; primary roles may not.
cast_model.determinism: Every cast draw uses world.rng.stream("narrative-cast"). Never Math.random.

quandamooka_households.rule: Quandamooka households are cast in exactly the same working and civic roles as any other household: ranger, health worker, deckhand, teacher aide, tradesperson, neighbour, council worker, volunteer, kid missing a boat. They are the largest part of Dunwich and leaving them out of the ordinary life of the island would be its own falsification.
hard_limits: No cast role carries cultural authority. There is no elder role, no knowledge holder role, no cultural guide role in this pack.
No seed generates ceremony, story, language, protocol, or a cultural position attributed to a person.

Where a real organisation would be the right actor (QYAC, MMEIC, Yulu-Burri-Ba, the joint management arrangement), the seed names it as an institution taking an institutional action already documented in data/civic.json, and never as a character with a view.
Anything beyond this goes to docs/CULTURAL-REVIEW.md before it is written, not after.

roles.one_line: Runs a boat and reads weather for a living.
Reads the water for food, not for a wage, and often for both.
roles.note: Distinct from the-skipper: the skipper runs a boat as a job, the fisher knows a gutter.

roles.one_line: Runs a venue and orders the stock.
Works whatever hours the season gives them.
Works on Country or in the park for wages.
Turns out when the pager goes, unpaid.
Answers the phone when something is hit.
Has been here longer than the argument.
Bought or moved in within the last few years and means well.
Housing is the whole plot whether or not the seed is about housing.
Crosses the bay for school or is about to.
Works at the primary school or supports it.
Clinic, ambulance, community health or in-home care.
Looks after someone at home, mostly unpaid.
Builds and fixes, and books the barge to do it.
Between the owner and the guest, and lives here.
Owns a house here and is here about twelve weekends a year.
roles.note: Tenure not_a_residence. Pays rates, votes elsewhere. Never written as a villain.

roles.one_line: Weeding on a Saturday for twenty years.
Carries a decision made somewhere else.
roles.note: The officer is never the antagonist. The officer is the person who has to say the thing out loud.

roles.one_line: Knows what everyone buys and when the barge missed.
Here for a day, a weekend or a fortnight, and does not know the rules yet.
Is going, or has gone, or is deciding.
Grew up here and is back, which is not the same as never having left.
Had a job that does not exist any more and has views about what replaced it.
Crosses the bay for work and lives by the timetable.

relationship_model.principle: Relationships are the only thing a story is allowed to change permanently. Everything else belongs to the systems.

dimensions.one_line: How much of each other's ordinary life they know.
dimensions.note: On an island of about two thousand people this starts high and moves slowly. Two long-term residents in the same township start above 0.6.

dimensions.one_line: Would you rely on them in a bad hour.
dimensions.note: Gains fast under shared load, loses fast on a broken promise, and recovers slower than it falls.

dimensions.one_line: Who owes who. Positive means A owes B.
dimensions.note: The real currency here. An unpaid obligation is the strongest single predictor of who turns up next time.
Decays fastest of the four, because you still see them at the shop. Halve the decay if the two households have had no contact event in the period.

change_rules.when: Two agents are cast in the same thread and both act in a consequence beat.
change_rules.note: Applies whether or not the thread ended well. Doing a hard thing together counts.

change_rules.when: One agent absorbs a cost that belonged to another: a shift, a lift, a bed, a tow, a phone call at two in the morning.
change_rules.effect: obligation +0.20 on the receiver, trust +0.10 both ways
change_rules.note: This is the engine. Most threads should create at least one of these.

change_rules.when: An agent with outstanding obligation is cast in a later thread and acts against their own interest.
change_rules.note: The director should preferentially cast agents with outstanding obligation. That is how a thread three months old pays off.

change_rules.when: An agent commits at a choice beat and the consequence beat shows they did not follow through.
change_rules.note: Only fires on an explicit commitment. Being unable to help is not the same as not turning up.

change_rules.when: Two agents take opposite sides at a civic beat with an audience.
change_rules.note: Deliberate: disagreeing at a meeting does not make islanders distrust each other. It makes Thursday slightly awkward.

change_rules.when: Same as public-disagreement, but one household has tenure not_a_residence or has lived here under three years.
change_rules.effect: friction +0.20 and trust -0.10 on the long-term side only
change_rules.note: Asymmetric on purpose. This is the actual shape of the argument on this island and the sim should not pretend otherwise.

change_rules.when: An agent is present at a slow-grief consequence beat involving another household.
change_rules.note: Grief lowers friction. Old arguments go quiet for a while.

change_rules.when: An agent from a household under three years on the island acts in a consequence beat of a thread they are not the subject of.
change_rules.effect: friction -0.15 with every long-term household in that township, familiarity +0.08
change_rules.note: The single fastest route from newcomer to local, and it is behavioural, not a timer.

change_rules.when: A thread ends and one agent carried more than half the consequence beats.
change_rules.effect: obligation +0.15 on every other cast member toward that agent, and that agent gains fatigue
change_rules.note: Feeds burnout in the volunteer roles, which is a real island failure mode.

change_rules.effect: familiarity decay rate x4, obligation frozen, trust unchanged
change_rules.note: Obligation is frozen rather than cleared. It is still owed if they come back.

negative.label: avoiding each other at the shop

hard_rules: A thread may never set a relationship value directly. It applies a named change rule, so the reason is inspectable.
Relationship state survives the thread that made it. Nothing resets at coda.
The player can inspect any pair and see the last three reasons a value moved. If the reason is not legible, the rule was wrong.
No agent tracks more than about 40 relationships in detail. Below that, hold a township-level familiarity floor and promote a pair to detailed tracking the first time they are cast together.

director.summary: The director picks what to run, and mostly picks nothing. Its job is to keep the island feeling inhabited without feeling written.

cadence.note: Six hours, not every tick. Nothing here needs ten minute resolution and the budget belongs to the simulation.

budgets.note: Four is the ceiling for a player to hold in their head. Two new a week means most weeks have one, and some have none.

cooldowns.note: Cooldowns are per save, deterministic, and stored. A seed that has never run is preferred over any seed that has.

order: Collect every seed whose trigger conditions are satisfied against current published state, skipping any seed with a missing required path.
Drop seeds on cooldown, seeds whose register budget is full, and seeds with no available cast.
Draw one using world.rng.stream("narrative") weighted by score, then apply the leave-space test before opening it.

score_terms.note: How far past the threshold the state actually is. A 4.2 m swell scores higher than a 3.1 m swell on the same seed.
Never run: 1.0. Run once, long ago: 0.5. Recently run: 0.0 and it was already filtered.
Prefer casting agents holding outstanding obligation, and agents who have not been in a thread. This is what makes month three pay off month one.
Inverse of that township's share of recent threads. Dunwich is the biggest township and will otherwise take everything.
Inverse of that register's share of the last ten threads. Stops the island reading as pure decline.

Slight preference for places and households the player has recently inspected, and a slight penalty for anything on screen right now. Being watched should not be a requirement, and it should not be a shield.
Per seed. Rare things stay rare.

leave_space_test.rule: After a thread closes, no new thread opens in that township for at least 3 sim-days. Across the island, at least 8 sim-days in every 30 must have no beat fire at all.
leave_space_test.why: An island where something happens every day is a soap. An island where nothing happens for a week and then two things happen at once is an island.

fizzle.rule: Every seed carries patience_days. If the next beat's required state does not arrive within that window, the thread closes as unresolved.
fizzle.note: About one thread in five should go nowhere. It is recorded in the chronicle as an open item, not as a failure, and it is eligible to reopen once after its cooldown. Some seeds are marked may_fizzle false because the state that opened them cannot un-happen.

hard_rules: The director never creates physical state. It cannot cancel a barge, raise a swell, kill a koala or empty a keg. It waits for a system to do that and then notices. Phase is narrative, which runs after environment, ecology, infrastructure, economy, agents, movement and civic, so everything it reads is settled for the tick.

Writes are limited to four channels: own (narrative state), social (relationship deltas via a named change rule), sentiment (interest group mood deltas, bounded), and intent (world.bus.emit("narrative:intent", ...), which another system may honour or ignore). A seed that needs a fifth channel is a system, not a seed.
No seed may require the player to act. Every seed has a quietly ending that runs with no input at all.
No thread may pile a second consequence on a household already in a slow-grief thread.
No two threads may cast the same primary household.
Every thread must be traceable: TWIN.probe().narrative lists the open threads, their seed id, their cast household ids, the beat they are on, and the state condition they are waiting for.
All randomness comes from world.rng.stream("narrative") and world.rng.stream("narrative-cast"). All timing comes from world.clock. Same seed and same inputs means the same stories.

Before a business, place, service or road is used in a thread, check it against its own pack. Skip anything whose status is closed or proposed. Anything trading-unconfirmed may be used only if the economy system has instantiated it; otherwise substitute another entry of the same type in the same township, and if there is none, skip the seed. A story must never be the thing that makes a business look real.

A seed may name a real organisation only where it is taking an action already documented for it in data/civic.json or data/businesses.json. It may never attribute a position, an opinion or a statement to a real organisation.
do_not: Do not run two seeds that need the same place on the same day.
Do not run a seed whose cause the player cannot currently see anywhere in the UI.
Do not resolve a structural problem. Erosion, the cost of crossing, the housing and the season do not get solved by a story.
Do not repeat a seed on the same household ever, even after cooldown.
Do not open a thread in the first three sim-days of a new save. Let the island be ordinary first.

endings_vocabulary.principle: Three shapes, and the third is the most common. A story that ends quietly is not a story that failed.
endings_vocabulary.well: Someone was carried. The problem is not fixed, but the person is all right and somebody owes somebody a favour.
endings_vocabulary.badly: The cost landed on the person least able to carry it, and everybody knows it. Never punitive to the player, never a game over.
endings_vocabulary.quietly: The weather changed, the boat ran, the thing did not happen, or it happened to somebody who did not tell anyone. One line in the chronicle and no fuss.
endings_vocabulary.unresolved: Written by the fizzle rule, not by a seed. The thread closes with its question still open and appears in the chronicle as an open item.

ratio_target.note: Measured over the last twenty closed threads. The director nudges scoring, not outcomes, to stay near this.

cultural_care.statement: Minjerribah is Quandamooka Country. This pack contains no cultural content: no language beyond what other packs already cite from published sources, no ceremony, no story, no sacred site, no protocol, and no words attributed to any person.
cultural_care.what_is_in_here: Quandamooka households appear the way the census says they appear: as roughly a quarter of the resident population, in ordinary jobs and ordinary situations, in every township and especially at Dunwich. Real organisations appear only as institutions taking actions already documented in data/civic.json and data/businesses.json.
open_questions_for_review: Whether the Quandamooka Festival season and NAIDOC Week should generate any narrative thread at all, or only civic load. This pack generates none and says so.

Whether joint management decisions in Naree Budjong Djara should ever appear as a thread with a Quandamooka household cast in it, or only as a policy state change with no cast. This pack does the second.

Whether the two items already routed to review under the ecology pack, the historic cooperative dolphin fishing at Amity Point and cultural burning, may ever be narrative material. This pack assumes not.
cultural_care.route: docs/CULTURAL-REVIEW.md, then a conversation with QYAC. Not a data decision.

seeds.title: The barge that did not run
seeds.one_line: A function is booked at Point Lookout for four in the afternoon and the boat that half the guests are on does not sail.
seeds.of_this_place: There is no bridge. Every guest, every crate of glasses and the celebrant all cross the same stretch of water on the same handful of sailings, and if one goes the next one is an hour away and already full.

conditions.note: venueId drawn from venues that hold functions: stradbroke-island-beach-hotel, point-lookout-bowls-club, amity-pavilion, little-ship-club, point-lookout-community-hall.
A cancellation with an empty apron is not a story.

also_requires.note: Friday, Saturday or Sunday. Functions do not happen on a Tuesday.

suppress_if.note: If everything is stopped this is a different seed: weather-holds-the-boats.

cast.why: Holds the booking, the food and the staff roster, and cannot move any of them.
Rostered for a four hour function that is now a seven hour one, or is now not happening at all.
The half of the party that is stuck at Toondah with a car full of chairs.
Running the walk-on boat, which is still going, and is the only reason anybody gets across.
Has a ute on the island and is the only person who can move the freight up from Junner Street.

beats.name: A normal Friday build
beats.what_happens: The venue sets up in the afternoon. Stock came over on an earlier sailing, staff are rostered, and one of the party is already on the island checking the room.
beats.legible: The venue shows a booked function and a staff roster in the inspector.
beats.chronicle: The bowls club set up for a function at four.

beats.name: The sailing is pulled
beats.what_happens: A vehicle sailing is cancelled. The vehicles on the apron roll to the next one, which is already booked, so the backlog is now longer than the afternoon.
beats.legible: The ferry panel shows the cancelled sailing and the vehicle backlog rising at Toondah.
beats.chronicle: The mid afternoon barge did not run and the backlog at Toondah went past sixty vehicles.

beats.name: Walk on or wait
beats.what_happens: The stuck half of the party can leave the cars at Cleveland and come over on the walk-on boat with what they can carry, or wait for a vehicle sailing that may not have room.

requires.note: The water taxi crossing is entirely inside the bay, so ocean swell is not a factor and it is usually still running when the barge is not.

sets.note: movement systems may honour or ignore

beats.legible: Two costs shown side by side: arrive late with everything, or arrive on time with almost nothing.
beats.chronicle: Half the party left the cars at Cleveland and came over on the water taxi.

beats.name: Somebody drives the ute
beats.what_happens: Whatever came over on the walk-on boat has to get from Junner Street to Point Lookout. Someone on the island with a vehicle does the run, twice, unpaid.
beats.legible: A vehicle runs the Dunwich to Point Lookout leg twice in an hour, visible on East Coast Road.
beats.chronicle: A ute did the Junner Street run twice and the function started about ninety minutes late.

beats.name: Late finish
beats.what_happens: The kitchen closes later than the roster allowed, the staff member misses the last bus, and the publican drives them home. Nobody mentions it again.
beats.legible: The staff member's fatigue is up and there is a new obligation edge in the relationship inspector.
beats.chronicle: The kitchen shut at eleven and the publican drove the cook home.

branches.question: Does the party split, or does it hold together and arrive late?

options.label: Leave the cars, take the water taxi
options.cost: Everything that needed a vehicle stays on the mainland.

options.label: Wait for a vehicle sailing
options.cost: Four hours on the apron and no guarantee of a place.
effects: half the party misses it entirely

options.label: Someone on the island brings a boat over
options.cost: Weather dependent, and it puts a private skipper in the middle of a commercial problem.

well.label: Late and fine
well.conditions: The function happens within three hours of the booked time.
well.chronicle: It ran late and it ran.

badly.label: Half a wedding
badly.conditions: Fewer than half the party arrives before the venue closes.
changes: friction between venue and ferry operator, which is a mood not a mechanic
badly.chronicle: Most of them never got over, and the venue refunded what it could.

quietly.label: The next one ran
quietly.conditions: The following sailing runs and clears the backlog before the booked time.
quietly.chronicle: The next barge ran and nobody had to do anything about it.

seeds.source: data/transport.json structural_facts no-bridge and busiest-days; SeaLink SEQ terms and conditions (20 minute vehicle check-in, no-show forfeit); data/transport.json note that the crossing is entirely inside the bay so swell is not a ferry factor.
seeds.notes: The specific wedding is fiction. The mechanism is not: one cancelled vehicle sailing on a Friday cascades because the next one is already sold.

seeds.title: The Gorge is shut
seeds.one_line: A school group comes over for the day and the swell closes the one thing they came for.
seeds.of_this_place: The North Gorge Walk is the island's single most visited thing and it sits on a headland that takes the full east swell. It has been closed before for erosion under the boardwalk. A bus of thirty children does not un-book.

conditions.note: Set by a coast or council system when swell plus tide overtops the low shelf, or after boardwalk damage.

cast.archetype_hint: mainland school, not Dunwich State School
cast.why: Responsible for thirty children and a return water taxi booking.
Put the barrier up this morning and has to stand next to it.
Thirty of them, and they can see the water from where they are standing.
Watching a crowd standing at a barrier above a big sea.
Suddenly has thirty children with four hours to fill.

beats.name: The 08:45 arrives
beats.what_happens: A school group lands at Dunwich and takes the bus to Point Lookout. The itinerary is the Gorge Walk, lunch at the headland, and the afternoon boat home.
beats.legible: A visitor group of thirty appears on the bus route and the headland crowd count starts climbing.
beats.chronicle: A school group came over on the morning boat and took the bus to Point Lookout.

beats.name: Barrier at the gate
beats.what_happens: The walk is closed. The swell is running over the low shelf and the council has shut the loop at both ends.
beats.legible: The walk renders closed, and the swell number in the weather panel is the reason.
beats.chronicle: The Gorge Walk was shut at both ends with the swell over three metres.

beats.name: Four hours to fill
beats.what_happens: The teacher can put the group on the beach at Cylinder inside the flags, take them back down to the museum at Dunwich, or try to bring the boat booking forward.
beats.legible: Three routes drawn on the map with the crowd load each one would put somewhere.
beats.chronicle: The group went looking for somewhere else to be.

beats.name: Wherever they go, they are thirty
beats.what_happens: The chosen place absorbs thirty extra people at once. The shop runs out of hot food, or the patrolled beach doubles its numbers, or the museum has a queue at the door.
beats.legible: The crowd count at the receiving place spikes and something there runs short.
beats.chronicle: Thirty of them ended up at the one place that could take them, and it ran out of pies.

beats.name: Somebody points at the sea
beats.what_happens: A local, doing something else, shows the group where the swell is breaking and what it is doing to the shelf. The excursion gets its lesson from the closure rather than despite it.
beats.legible: Visitor satisfaction recovers most of what it lost.
beats.chronicle: Someone showed them where the swell was breaking and that turned out to be the excursion.

branches.question: Where do thirty children go?

options.label: Cylinder Beach inside the flags
options.cost: Doubles the load on the patrol on a big day.

options.label: Back down to the museum
options.cost: An hour of the day on a bus, and the museum is small.
effects: small revenue to a volunteer-run venue

options.label: Try to move the boat booking forward
options.cost: The earlier sailing is a commuter one and there may not be seats.

well.label: A different day out
well.conditions: The group ends up somewhere that could hold them and someone local explains the closure.
changes: a small business has a good day
well.chronicle: They saw the wrong thing and it was better.

badly.label: Standing at a barrier
badly.conditions: The group spends more than two hours with nowhere to go.
badly.chronicle: They stood at the barrier for two hours and got the boat home early.

quietly.label: Went to the beach
quietly.chronicle: They went to the beach instead.

seeds.source: Redland City Bulletin, section of the Point Lookout Gorge Walk closed after erosion (https://www.redlandcitybulletin.com.au/story/7225935/gorge-walk-section-closed-after-erosion/); Redlands Coast Today, Point Lookout Gorge Walk update (https://news.redland.qld.gov.au/2021/06/point-lookout-gorge-walk-update-still-great-viewing/); data/places.json north-gorge-walk; data/events.json visitor archetype school-group.
seeds.notes: The documented closures were caused by rainfall damaging boardwalk foundations, not directly by swell. A swell-driven closure of the low shelf is a modelling assumption and is marked medium. If council only ever closes it for structural damage, change the trigger to a damage path and keep the rest.

seeds.title: Another two metres
seeds.one_line: A house at Amity Point comes back from a weekend away to less yard than it had.
seeds.of_this_place: Amity Point is losing shoreline to episodic flow slides and the migration of the Rainbow Channel. It is a declared erosion prone area. Land that has gone includes public and private land and, historically, the old racecourse, which is now out under the channel.

conditions.note: Relative movement, not an absolute rate. No published metres per year exists for this shoreline.

cast.why: Has watched the line move for forty years and can point at where the fence used to be.
Was not here when it happened, pays rates, and cannot vote in the council that decides.
Brings the shoreline erosion management plan and the word that private land is a private responsibility.
Quotes the rock, and knows what it costs to get rock onto this island.
Bought two doors up eighteen months ago and did not read the coastal hazard overlay.

beats.name: The usual line
beats.what_happens: An ordinary week at Amity. Someone walks the beach at low tide the way they do every day and the shoreline is where it was.
beats.legible: The shoreline is drawn and the beach width metric has a value.
beats.chronicle: The beach at Amity was where it usually is.

beats.name: It goes at night
beats.what_happens: A flow slide takes a section of the bank. There is no storm, no warning and no noise anybody heard. Some yard, a bit of fence, and part of the access down to the sand.
beats.legible: The shoreline geometry moves, the beach width metric drops, and the affected properties are highlighted.
beats.chronicle: A section of bank went overnight and took about two metres of yard with it.

beats.name: Rock, sand, or nothing
beats.what_happens: The owner can pay for rock protection on private land, join a shared nourishment effort, or do nothing and see what the next one takes. Council has a plan, a budget, and a boundary between public and private that is exactly where this argument sits.
beats.legible: Three costs shown: private rock, a share of nourishment, and the expected loss over five years of doing nothing.
beats.chronicle: The choice was rock, sand, or wait and see.

beats.name: The neighbour effect
beats.what_happens: Whatever one property does changes what happens next door. Rock on one lot moves the energy along the reach. Doing nothing on one lot leaves a notch that works back behind the neighbour.
beats.legible: The adjacent property risk value changes as a direct result of the decision on this one.
beats.chronicle: What one place did showed up next door within a season.

beats.name: Where the fence used to be
beats.what_happens: Somebody who has been here long enough walks the beach and points out where the fence line, the track and the old buildings used to be. Nothing is resolved. The shoreline keeps going.
beats.legible: A historical shoreline overlay becomes available to the player from this point on.
beats.chronicle: They walked the beach and someone said where the fence used to be.

branches.question: Who pays to hold a private shoreline?

options.label: Owner pays for rock
options.cost: Tens of thousands, and every tonne of rock crosses on the barge.

options.label: Council-led beach nourishment
options.cost: Recurrent budget, and it has to be repeated.

options.label: Managed retreat
options.cost: Politically the hardest thing on the island, and it is somebody's house.
effects: consultation_trust -0.10 if done without the consultation lever

options.label: Nothing
options.cost: Free this year.
effects: thread eligible to reopen after cooldown

well.label: Sand back on the beach
well.conditions: A nourishment or research lever is enacted within the thread window.
changes: the problem returns on its own schedule
well.chronicle: Sand went back on the beach and everyone knew it was temporary.

badly.label: The notch
badly.conditions: Nothing is done and a second flow slide fires within the window.
changes: a dwelling becomes uninhabitable, which is a housing system event, not a narrative one
badly.chronicle: The second one took the corner of the slab.

quietly.label: A fence and a quote
quietly.conditions: Default. The owner puts up a temporary fence and gets a quote they do not act on.
changes: the highlighted risk stays on the map
quietly.chronicle: They fenced it off and got a quote and left it at that.

seeds.source: Redland City Council Amity Point Shoreline Erosion Management Plan and Your Say Redlands Coast consultation (https://yoursay.redland.qld.gov.au/amity-point-shoreline-erosion); Amity Point Shoreline Erosion Study draft report (https://www.redland.qld.gov.au/files/assets/public/v/1/roads-and-marine/marine-facilities-permits-and-licences/amity-point-semp/amity-point-semp-central-reach/documents/shoreline-erosion-study-draft-2015.pdf); data/ecology.json proc-amity-erosion; data/civic.json amity-erosion issue.
seeds.notes: Two metres is the story's number, not a published rate. No metres-per-year figure, flow slide frequency or nourishment volume is published for this shoreline, which is why the trigger is relative. Do not let a UI panel state an erosion rate.

seeds.title: On East Coast Road
seeds.one_line: A koala is hit on the road between Dunwich and Point Lookout, and the person who stops is not the person who hit it.
seeds.of_this_place: This island's koalas have been genetically isolated for thousands of years and vehicle strike is the top recorded mortality cause. East Coast Road is the one road that connects everything, and its speed was cut from 100 to 80 to help.

season_bias.note: Spring breeding and dispersal is the road strike peak.

also_requires.note: Dispersal is when they cross roads.

cast.why: On the phone list, and has done this before, which does not make it easier.
Was driving to the beach at dusk and did not know koalas cross here.
Records it, because the record is the only reason anyone knows the number.
Stops because they always stop, and has an opinion about the speed limit.
In the back seat of the car that stopped.

beats.name: Dusk on the road
beats.what_happens: Traffic on East Coast Road at the end of the day: campers heading back, a bus, a work ute. The light is going and the speed is what it always is.
beats.legible: Traffic volume and mean speed on East Coast Road are visible, and the koala layer shows animals near the verge.
beats.chronicle: The road was busy at dusk the way it is at the end of a hot day.

beats.name: On the verge
beats.what_happens: A strike. The vehicle that did it keeps going, probably without knowing. The next car stops.
beats.legible: The road strike counter increments and a marker appears at the location.
beats.chronicle: A koala was hit on East Coast Road near dusk and the car behind stopped.

beats.name: Who is coming
beats.what_happens: The volunteer rescue line is a phone number and a person who has to drive there. If the animal is alive, the next question is whether there is anyone on the island who can treat it or whether it has to cross the bay.
beats.legible: A callout appears with a response time, and the response time depends on whether the rescue lever is funded.
beats.chronicle: The rescue number was called and someone drove out from Dunwich.

beats.name: The crossing that is not there
beats.what_happens: It goes either way, and either way it lands on the same volunteer. Afterwards somebody looks up whether this stretch was in the crossings proposal, and it was, and it is not funded.
beats.legible: The unfunded lever gets a visible pressure marker in the civic panel.
beats.chronicle: The stretch was on the crossings list and the crossings list is not funded.

beats.name: One more on the sheet
beats.what_happens: The volunteer adds it to the sheet. The sheet is the population data. That is the whole monitoring system for this animal on this island, and everybody who does it knows that.
beats.legible: The koala road death count for the year updates in the ecology panel.
beats.chronicle: It went on the sheet, which is how anybody knows the number at all.

branches.question: Is there capacity to treat it here?

options.label: Treated on the island
options.cost: Depends entirely on whether the wildlife rescue lever is funded.
effects: animal survives with probability set by ecology system

options.label: Goes to the mainland
options.cost: A volunteer drives to Dunwich, waits for a boat, and drives to Brisbane and back.
effects: obligation created toward that volunteer across the township

options.label: Too late
options.cost: Nothing to decide.

well.label: It made it
well.conditions: The animal is treated and released.
well.chronicle: It was released back near where it was found about three weeks later.

badly.label: The count goes up
badly.conditions: The animal dies and no lever moves.
badly.chronicle: It did not make it, and the count for the year went up by one.

quietly.label: A drive to Brisbane
quietly.conditions: Default. Someone loses a day and nobody hears about it.
quietly.chronicle: Someone drove it to the mainland and got the late boat back.

seeds.source: Recorded koala mortality on this island for 1997 to 2010: vehicle strike 35, disease 21, dog attack 16, from the study North Stradbroke Island: an island ark for Queensland's koala population? (https://www.researchgate.net/publication/233810684_North_Stradbroke_Island_an_island_ark_for_Queensland's_koala_population), also carried in data/ecology.json sp-koala; Redland City Bulletin, North Stradbroke Island road speed reduced from 100 to 80 km/h to improve safety for road users and wildlife (https://www.redlandcitybulletin.com.au/story/5332148/north-stradbroke-island-road-speed-to-be-reduced/); data/civic.json wildlife-speed-and-crossings and wildlife-rescue-support levers; data/businesses.json wildlife-rescue-minjerribah.
seeds.notes: No island-wide koala population figure exists in public, so this seed never states one. It states the road death count, which is the number that actually gets recorded. Whether there is on-island veterinary capacity is unconfirmed: straddie-mobile-vet is trading-unconfirmed in the businesses pack, so the branch reads capacity from state rather than assuming it.

seeds.title: The pub runs dry
seeds.one_line: It is the Saturday of a long weekend, the island is full, and the beer that was meant to come over on Thursday did not.
seeds.of_this_place: Everything drunk, eaten or built on this island came across on a boat. A missed freight sailing on a Thursday is invisible until Saturday night, when there is no second delivery and no shop on the mainland you can duck to.

conditions.note: venueId from licensed venues: stradbroke-island-beach-hotel, point-lookout-bowls-club, the-point-bar-and-bistro, amity-pavilion, little-ship-club, straddie-sharks-all-sports-club, straddie-brewing-co, amity-point-community-club.
Modelled threshold. No published peak island population exists.

cast.why: Ordered it, chased it, and is now the person telling a full room.
Has stock, is not licensed for what is wanted, and is about to have a very good and very stressful evening.
Behind the bar explaining it about four hundred times.
Genuinely does not understand why you cannot just get more.
Finds this funny, and remembers when it happened at Easter years ago.

beats.name: Ordering for a big one
beats.what_happens: The venue orders up for a long weekend. The order is bigger than usual and it has to be on a specific sailing to be here in time.
beats.legible: The venue shows an inbound delivery on the freight schedule.
beats.chronicle: The pub ordered up big for the long weekend.

beats.name: It did not come
beats.what_happens: The delivery does not arrive. It is on the mainland, or it is on the wrong sailing, or it did not get loaded. Nobody notices until stock levels fall through on Saturday afternoon.
beats.legible: Stock lines go red in the business inspector while the crowd count is still climbing.
beats.chronicle: The delivery never came and by five o'clock two taps were off.

beats.name: Ring around
beats.what_happens: The publican can ring the other venues and buy stock off them at cost, send someone on the water taxi with a trolley, or put the sign up and wear it.
beats.legible: Three options with a cost each and a visible effect on the other venue's stock.
beats.chronicle: They started ringing around.

beats.name: Whoever helps is short on Sunday
beats.what_happens: Any venue that lends stock is short itself the following day, which is the Sunday of a long weekend. The favour is real and expensive.
beats.legible: The lending venue's stock goes red on Sunday and the chain is traceable in the chronicle.
beats.chronicle: The club lent them four kegs and ran out themselves on the Sunday.

beats.name: The Tuesday delivery
beats.what_happens: The stock arrives on Tuesday when the island is empty again. Somebody puts a note on the order sheet about which sailing to book next time, and next year it happens to somebody else.
beats.legible: Freight arrives on the first quiet sailing and stock returns to normal.
beats.chronicle: It turned up Tuesday, when there was nobody here to drink it.

branches.question: Do you ask the other venues?

options.label: Buy stock off the club
options.cost: You owe them, and they will be short tomorrow.
effects: both venues take a small viability hit

options.label: Send someone over on the boat
options.cost: A staff member loses their evening and there is a limit to what a person can carry.

options.label: Put the sign up
options.cost: A full room and nothing to sell them.
effects: the other venues have a very good night

well.label: Borrowed from the club
well.conditions: Stock is transferred and the room is served.
well.chronicle: They got through on borrowed stock and owed the club one.

badly.label: The sign on the taps
badly.conditions: No transfer and the venue runs out before nine.
badly.chronicle: The taps went off at nine and the room went somewhere else.

quietly.label: Nobody noticed
quietly.conditions: Only one line runs out and there is a substitute.
quietly.chronicle: They ran out of one thing and sold something else.

seeds.source: data/transport.json structural_facts no-bridge and busiest-days; data/transport.json freight gap note; data/businesses.json licensed venues; data/events.json long-weekends period.
seeds.notes: The freight mechanism is documented in outline only. No tonnage, sailing allocation or delivery schedule for island freight is published, and stradbrokeislandcarriers.com.au would not resolve on 7 August 2026. The seed fires on relative stock state rather than an assumed delivery calendar.

seeds.title: The shack sells
seeds.one_line: A fibro place that has been in one family since before the mine sells in eleven days to somebody from Brisbane, and it will not be a rental again.
seeds.of_this_place: Permanent rentals on this island have been drying up while short stay listings sit in the hundreds. A single sale is not a housing crisis, but on an island this size it is one house, one family, and about four per cent of that township's rental stock.

season_bias.note: Winter listing, spring settlement, ready for summer letting.

conditions.note: Relative to township stock. The number matters less than the direction.

cast.why: Has lived in it for six years, works on the island, and has ninety days.
Selling it, because the estate has to be split three ways and none of the three live here.
Will be managing it in four months, and is friends with the person being evicted.
Employs the renter, or is employed by the same place, and is doing the arithmetic on whether they can stay either.
The buyer. Not a villain. Wanted a place near the water for their kids the way everyone here once did.

beats.name: A house that has always been let
beats.what_happens: An ordinary rental with a long tenancy. The renter works locally, the kid is at the school, the rent is under market because the owner never put it up.
beats.legible: The dwelling shows a long tenancy and a below-market rent in the housing inspector.
beats.chronicle: The house had been let to the same family for six years.

beats.name: A sign at the gate
beats.what_happens: It goes on the market. The photographs are taken with the tenants' furniture in them. The inspections are on Saturdays.
beats.legible: The dwelling changes status and a sale marker appears on the map.
beats.chronicle: It went on the market in June with the tenants still in it.

beats.name: Where do you go
beats.what_happens: There is nothing to rent. The choices are a share house at the wrong end of the island, a caravan on someone's block, the mainland, or asking the employer whether there is a bed.
beats.legible: The available rentals list is visibly, checkably empty.
beats.chronicle: There were two rentals listed on the whole island and both were holiday lets.

beats.name: The job goes with the house
beats.what_happens: If the household leaves, their job leaves with them, and it is a job the island cannot easily fill: a cleaner, a teacher aide, a support worker, a cook. The vacancy sits open.
beats.legible: A job vacancy opens and stays open, and a business shows staffShort.
beats.chronicle: The job they did stayed open for two months and then the shift just stopped existing.

beats.name: Clean and empty
beats.what_happens: The house is repainted and photographed. It sleeps eight. It is empty about two hundred nights a year and full on every long weekend.
beats.legible: The dwelling reappears as short stay stock and the township's occupancy pattern changes shape.
beats.chronicle: By November it was listed as sleeping eight, and it was empty most weeknights.

branches.question: Does the household stay on the island?

options.label: The employer finds a bed
options.cost: Only possible if worker accommodation exists. Ties the household's home to their job.
effects: obligation on the household toward the employer, which is its own problem

options.label: A community housing place comes up
options.cost: Rare, and it takes somebody else's place in the queue.

options.label: A caravan on a mate's block
options.cost: Not lawful under the planning scheme, and everyone knows.

options.label: They go
options.cost: The island loses a household, a worker and a kid off the school roll.

well.label: They found something
well.conditions: The household is still on the island 120 days after the sale.
well.chronicle: They got a place at the other end of the island and the kid stayed at the school.

badly.label: Gone by October
badly.conditions: The household leaves.
badly.chronicle: They loaded a trailer onto the barge on a Tuesday and that was that.

quietly.label: A caravan and a promise
quietly.conditions: Default. They stay, informally, and nobody records it.
changes: the household is now flagged insecure
quietly.chronicle: They put a caravan on a mate's block and said it was for a few weeks.

seeds.source: data/residents.json household archetypes with tenure not_a_residence and the 2021 census unoccupied dwelling share; data/civic.json housing issue and its seven levers; reporting that permanent rental options on the island have dried up and long-term residents including young families have left, cited in the Queensland short-term letting debate; Stayz lists more than 295 short-term rentals for North Stradbroke Island.
seeds.notes: No current median price or rental count for the island was verified, so no price is stated anywhere in this seed. The trigger uses listings and short stay share, which the housing system can compute internally, rather than a dollar figure.

seeds.title: A calf in the wrong place
seeds.one_line: A water taxi skipper on the morning run sees a cow and calf inside the channel, and the rules say one thing while the timetable says another.
seeds.of_this_place: The humpback migration passes this headland twice a year and the southbound run comes close inshore with calves. The commuter boats cross the bay on a timetable that school students and shift workers depend on, and a calf inside the caution zone is a legal problem, a safety problem and a rostering problem at once.

season_bias.note: Southbound with calves peaks about October.

also_requires.note: In a chop you do not see them until you are on them, which is a different and worse seed.

cast.why: Has a licence, a timetable and a boat full of people who have to be somewhere.
On the boat, has a meeting, is watching a whale and a clock at the same time.
On the same boat, going to school on the mainland, and this will be the story at lunch.
Takes the report. The report is data.
Paid for a tour and is now seeing more from a commuter boat than the tour gets.

beats.name: The 07:00 crossing
beats.what_happens: An ordinary weekday crossing. Students, a couple of tradies, someone going to an appointment. About twenty five minutes.
beats.legible: The water taxi is drawn on its route with a passenger load.
beats.chronicle: The seven o'clock boat went out with about forty on board.

beats.name: Blow, close
beats.what_happens: A cow and calf, inside the caution zone, on the line the boat runs. The skipper throttles back. Under the Queensland rules a vessel inside 300 metres of a whale must not do more than six knots, and a calf tightens everything.
beats.legible: The vessel speed drops and an ETA slips in the transport panel.
beats.chronicle: A cow and calf came up on the line and the boat came back to idle.

beats.name: Wait or go around
beats.what_happens: Sit and wait for them to move, or take a longer line and arrive late. Both cost time, and the second one costs fuel and a connection at the other end.
beats.legible: Two arrival times shown, and the connecting bus on the mainland side is visible in one of them and not the other.
beats.chronicle: The skipper took the long way round.

beats.name: The connection at the other end
beats.what_happens: The boat is eight minutes late. Two students miss the school bus. One passenger misses a specialist appointment that took three months to get and cannot be moved.
beats.legible: Individual agents show a missed connection and an unmet need.
beats.chronicle: The boat was eight minutes late and two kids missed the bus at Cleveland.

beats.name: It goes in the log
beats.what_happens: The sighting is logged. Somebody at the club puts it on the board. The whale watchers up on the headland saw the same pair an hour later from land, for nothing.
beats.legible: The whale sighting count for the day increments and the headland crowd rises for the rest of the week.
beats.chronicle: The pair went past the headland about nine and half of Point Lookout saw them for free.

branches.question: Timetable or distance?

options.label: Sit and wait
options.cost: Late, and the lateness lands on whoever had the tightest connection.

options.label: Take a wider line
options.cost: Later still, and more fuel.

options.label: Hold the line and hold speed
options.cost: Unlawful inside the caution zone, and the boat is full of witnesses.

well.label: Everyone got where they were going
well.conditions: Delay under ten minutes and no unmet need.
well.chronicle: It cost nine minutes and everyone thought it was worth it.

badly.label: The appointment
badly.conditions: A high-stakes unmet need lands.
changes: a household carries a real cost
badly.chronicle: The specialist appointment had taken three months to get and there was no later one.

quietly.label: A slow crossing
quietly.chronicle: The boat was late and nobody minded much.

seeds.source: Queensland rules for watching marine mammals: no approach zone of 100 m around a whale extending 300 m front and behind, caution zone to 300 m with a six knot limit, and a 300 m rule around calves in Commonwealth waters (https://www.qld.gov.au/environment/plants-animals/animals/discovering-wildlife/watching-wildlife/watching-marine-mammals/rules-for-watching-marine-mammals); data/ecology.json proc-whale-season and sp-humpback-whale; data/transport.json water taxi services and the 25 minute crossing.
seeds.notes: The exact distances differ between Queensland waters, the Moreton Bay Marine Park and Commonwealth waters, and a real skipper would know which applies where. The seed states the caution zone and the six knot limit only, which are consistent across the sources read.

seeds.title: The working bee and the dog
seeds.one_line: Eleven people turn up to pull weeds and by the second hour it is a conversation about the off lead area, again.
seeds.of_this_place: Dog attack is the third recorded cause of koala death on this island, dogs are prohibited from the national park and from Brown Lake, and there is a small number of off lead areas. Everyone at the working bee agrees about weeds. Nobody agrees about dogs.

cast.why: Has been doing this Saturday morning for nineteen years and has a folder.
Came to help, brought the dog, tied it up properly, and is about to become an example.
Has always had dogs here and does not think a lead on a beach is what saved anything.
Came to drop off gloves and is now in an unpaid consultation.
Has picked up what a dog did and does not want to say so on a Saturday morning.

beats.name: Gloves and a thermos
beats.what_happens: A working bee. Weeds out, mulch down, morning tea at ten. Eleven people, mostly the same eleven.
beats.legible: A small crowd appears at the site and the vegetation condition of that patch is visibly improving.
beats.chronicle: Eleven turned up with gloves and one of them brought a thermos.

beats.name: The dog comes up
beats.what_happens: Somebody mentions an incident. Something on the beach, or a koala, or a bird roost. The conversation stops being about weeds.
beats.legible: The dog incident metric is visible and rising in the civic panel.
beats.chronicle: Somebody brought up what happened at the roost and that was the rest of the morning.

beats.name: Say it or let it go
beats.what_happens: Two people can have the argument properly in front of everyone, or they can leave it and finish the weeds. Both are real options and the group is split about evenly.
beats.legible: The consultation submission counter for the off lead review moves if the argument happens.
beats.chronicle: It got said out loud, which does not happen often.

beats.name: Two fewer next month
beats.what_happens: The group finishes the patch. Next month two people do not come. One of them is the person who was right.

sets.condition: if one household is under three years on the island

beats.legible: Working bee attendance drops the following month and the vegetation condition improvement slows.
beats.chronicle: The next working bee had nine.

beats.name: A submission goes in
beats.what_happens: Somebody writes a submission to the off lead area review, which is open. It is one of eleven. It does not change anything by itself and it goes on the record, which is the point.
beats.legible: A submission appears against the lever and the consultation trust metric moves slightly.
beats.chronicle: One submission went in before the review closed.

branches.question: Does anybody say it?

options.label: Have the argument
options.cost: Two regulars stop coming and it is awkward at the shop for a month.

options.label: Change the subject

options.label: Ask the officer to bring it back formally
options.cost: Slow, and it turns neighbours into submitters.

well.chronicle: It ended up as a submission, which is slower and works better.

badly.label: Nine next month

badly.chronicle: Two of them stopped coming and nothing went on the record.

quietly.chronicle: Somebody changed the subject and the mulch went down by eleven.

seeds.title: One less on the boat
seeds.one_line: A nineteen year old packs a car onto the barge, and everyone at the ramp knows they are not coming back for a while.
seeds.of_this_place: The secondary department at Dunwich State School closed in 2012 with six students, so every island teenager already crosses the bay every day. Leaving properly is a short trip and a permanent one, and it is the ordinary thing that happens, not a tragedy.

season_bias.note: End of the school year and the start of the university year.

cast.why: Nineteen. Has worked three summers in hospitality and there is no fourth thing here.
The parent or grandparent. Is proud and is not going to say the other thing.
Was going to roster them for summer and now has a hole.
Two years younger and now doing the same arithmetic.
Has watched about thirty of these and still comes down to the ramp.

beats.name: The last summer
beats.what_happens: A young person working a season: shifts at a venue, weekends at the beach, everyone knows their name and their car.
beats.legible: The agent appears on a roster and at the same three places all summer.
beats.chronicle: They worked the whole summer and were at the beach every day off.

beats.name: Nothing next
beats.what_happens: The season ends. The shifts drop from about sixty hours to about twenty. There is no course here, no apprenticeship here, and nothing to rent that is not a share of a room.
beats.legible: The agent's rostered hours fall in the jobs panel and their income goes under their costs.
beats.chronicle: After Australia Day the shifts went from sixty hours to twenty.

beats.name: Stay on less, or go
beats.what_happens: Stay and live on winter hours in a share house, or take a full time job or a course on the mainland. The second one is obviously correct and that is what makes it hard.
beats.legible: Two forecasts side by side: island income against mainland income, with the crossing cost in both.
beats.chronicle: The mainland job paid nearly twice as much and did not stop in March.

beats.name: The ramp
beats.what_happens: A car with everything in it goes onto the barge on a weekday morning. Four or five people come down for it, which is what happens here.
beats.legible: The permanent population ticks down by one and the agent leaves the world.
beats.chronicle: The car went on the nine o'clock barge and about five people came down to the ramp.

beats.name: The gap in the team
beats.what_happens: The football side or the fishing club or the roster is one short. It is filled or it is not. Nobody says the word exodus, because it is one person.
beats.legible: A club or roster shows a persistent gap that a later thread can pick up.
beats.chronicle: The side played a man short for the first three rounds.

branches.question: Is there a reason to stay?

options.label: A year-round job exists
options.cost: Requires the island economy to have a job that does not stop in March.
effects: that job now cannot be filled by someone else

options.label: Somewhere to live alone
options.cost: Requires worker housing or a community housing place.

options.label: They go
options.cost: Ordinary and permanent.
effects: the household is now split across the bay

options.label: They go, saying it is for a year
options.cost: Sets up the homecoming seed to run in twelve to thirty six months.
effects: flags the agent as a candidate for someone-comes-home

well.label: A reason to stay
well.conditions: A job or a bed appears within the window.
well.chronicle: They got the council job and stayed, and everyone acted like it was nothing.

badly.label: Gone
badly.conditions: The household loses a member and nothing replaces the skill.
changes: a club or roster is short
badly.chronicle: They went in February and the side played short until June.

quietly.label: For a year
quietly.conditions: Default. Framed as temporary by everyone including the leaver.
changes: the agent is flagged for a possible return
quietly.chronicle: They said it was for a year.

seeds.source: Redland City Bulletin, Dunwich high school closes its doors: the Year 8 to 10 secondary department at Dunwich closed in 2012 and its six students moved to Cleveland District State High School, with transport subsidies for island secondary students (https://www.redlandcitybulletin.com.au/story/247451/dunwich-high-school-closes-its-doors/); data/residents.json occupation secondary-student-mainland and the seasonal-hospitality archetypes; data/civic.json cost-of-living and housing issues.
seeds.notes: No island out-migration figure is published. The seed fires on the simulation's own leaver count moving, never on a claimed real-world rate.

seeds.title: Someone comes home
seeds.one_line: Somebody who grew up here comes back with a trade, a kid and no idea how much the rent is now.
seeds.of_this_place: People come back to this island. That is not sentiment, it is the census: three generation households at Dunwich are one of the largest archetypes here. The complication is that the place they are coming back to has a housing market shaped by people who do not live here.

conditions.note: They are coming back into a real gap.

also_requires.note: Preferred but not required. If a leaver from a previous thread is still alive in the save, cast them.

cast.why: Left at nineteen, is back at thirty two, and the island did not stay still.
The reason they came back, usually. Somebody needs somebody.
Remembers them as a kid and will keep calling them that.
Has more work than hands and wants to know if they are staying.
Is competing with them for the same two listings, and likes them.

beats.name: A vacancy nobody can fill
beats.what_happens: A job on the island has been open long enough that people have stopped mentioning it: a chippy, a health worker, a mechanic, a bus driver.
beats.legible: A vacancy in the jobs panel with a long unfilled counter.
beats.chronicle: The job had been open since March.

beats.name: They come back
beats.what_happens: Somebody arrives with a trade certificate and a kid for the school. Everybody is pleased. There is nowhere for them to live.
beats.legible: A new household enters the world with a filled job and no dwelling.
beats.chronicle: They came back in April with a trade ticket and nowhere to live.

beats.name: Whose spare room
beats.what_happens: Move in with family, which works and does not, or take something at the wrong end of the island, or put a second dwelling on family land, which needs an approval.
beats.legible: Three housing options with a household crowding number, a commute cost, and an approval lead time.
beats.chronicle: They moved in with family, which everyone said was temporary.

beats.name: Three generations in a three bedroom
beats.what_happens: The household is now crowded. It also now has a driver, a carer and an income under one roof, which solves four other problems and creates two.
beats.legible: The household's crowding and stress rise while its transport and care coverage improve.
beats.chronicle: There were seven in the house and someone was always on the couch.

beats.name: Still here at Christmas
beats.what_happens: They are still here at Christmas. Somebody at the club stops calling them by their childhood name. The second dwelling application is either approved or still in the queue.
beats.legible: The household persists past 180 days, or it does not.
beats.chronicle: They were still here at Christmas, which is longer than most people gave it.

branches.question: Can the island house someone it needs?

options.label: A second dwelling on family land
options.cost: An approval, a build, and every load of material on the barge.
effects: rental_supply unchanged but a household housed

options.label: Move in with family
options.cost: Crowding, and it is not temporary.
effects: the household is invisible in any housing statistic

options.label: A rental at the other end of the island
options.cost: A commute on a road with no footpath, and the school run gets harder.

options.label: They go back
options.cost: The job stays open and the island keeps the gap.

well.label: Housed and working
well.conditions: The household has its own dwelling and the job stays filled at 180 days.
well.chronicle: The shed out the back got a bathroom and that was that.

badly.label: Back across the bay
badly.conditions: The household leaves within 120 days.
badly.chronicle: They lasted five months and went back to the mainland for a house.

quietly.label: On the couch
quietly.chronicle: They stayed at his mum's, which everyone kept calling temporary.

seeds.source: data/residents.json household_archetypes quandamooka-family-multigenerational-dunwich and ex-mine-worker-couple-dunwich; data/civic.json housing levers including secondary-dwelling-fast-track and community-housing-expansion.
seeds.notes: Deliberately paired with one-less-on-the-boat. If a leaver agent from an earlier thread is still tracked, the director should cast that agent here rather than generating a new one. That is the single highest value connection in this pack.

seeds.title: The count is down
seeds.one_line: The people who watch the headland every winter morning say there are fewer going past this week, and they are right, and it does not mean what the pub thinks it means.
seeds.of_this_place: This headland is one of the best land-based whale watching points on the east coast and half the winter economy is built on it. A quiet week off the point is a weather and distance story, not a population story: the east Australian humpback population has been increasing at about ten per cent a year for decades.

cast.why: Walks up every morning in winter and keeps a count in a notebook. Has done it for years.
Books staff on winter whale trade and can see the tables.
Came for two days, saw nothing, is not angry, is just disappointed in a way that is worse.
Puts it on the community page as a disaster and gets corrected by six people.
Knows the difference between a quiet week and a trend and says so in one sentence.

beats.name: The morning walk
beats.what_happens: Winter mornings at the headland. Twenty or thirty people on the walk before eight, and someone counting.
beats.legible: A headland crowd count and a whale sighting count both visible each morning.
beats.chronicle: There were thirty on the headland before eight, the way there always is in July.

beats.name: Four days of nothing much
beats.what_happens: The seven day mean drops well under normal for the date. There is a reason and it is boring: they are further out, or the wind is wrong, or the water is dirty.
beats.legible: The whale sighting graph shows the seven day mean against the seasonal band.
beats.chronicle: Four mornings running the count was under half what it should be for the date.

beats.name: What do you tell people
beats.what_happens: The businesses and the volunteers can say it is a quiet week, or they can let the word go around that the whales are gone. One of those is true and the other one travels faster.
beats.legible: Two visitor demand forecasts, one for each framing.
beats.chronicle: Somebody put it on the community page and the word went around fast.

beats.name: Bookings for August
beats.what_happens: The framing moves next month's bookings more than the actual whales do. If the wrong story wins, winter trade drops for three weeks and then the whales come back and nobody rebooks.
beats.legible: Visitor archetype counts for whale-watcher fall or hold, and the businesses that depend on them show it.
beats.chronicle: August bookings came off about a fifth and the whales were back inside a week.

beats.name: The notebook
beats.what_happens: The person with the notebook has ten years of counts in it and can show that this happens most winters. Nobody has ever asked to see it before.
beats.legible: The player gains a multi-year sighting history overlay from this thread.
beats.chronicle: They had ten years of it in a notebook and it happened most winters.

branches.question: Which story goes around?

options.label: It is a quiet week
options.cost: Boring, and it requires somebody to be trusted.

options.label: The whales are gone
options.cost: Three weeks of winter trade, and it is not true.

options.label: Nobody says anything
options.cost: The week passes and so does the worry.

well.label: A quiet week
well.conditions: The correct framing holds and bookings do not move.
changes: trust in a long-term resident rises
well.chronicle: It was a quiet week and then it was not.

badly.label: Three weeks of empty tables
badly.conditions: The wrong framing wins.
changes: staff hours cut in winter, which is when people can least afford it
badly.chronicle: August came off a fifth and by the time they were back it was too late to rebook.

quietly.label: They came back
quietly.chronicle: They were back by the weekend.

seeds.source: data/ecology.json proc-whale-season; east Australian humpback population increasing at about ten to eleven per cent a year and now estimated around 50,000, from International Whaling Commission scientific committee papers and the 2025 ORRCA census reporting (https://iwc.int/public/documents/AqlSh/SC-63-SH22.pdf); data/events.json whale-season period.
seeds.notes: This seed exists partly to stop the simulation teaching a false thing. The brief asked for a seed where the whale count is down. The honest version is that a local count being down is normal and the population trend is strongly up, and the drama is in what people do with an ambiguous number. No island-specific sighting count is published, so the seasonal norm must be the simulation's own, not a claimed real one.

seeds.title: The fish are on
seeds.one_line: Word goes around at about four in the afternoon and by dark there are forty vehicles on the beach.
seeds.of_this_place: Tailor in the gutters off Main Beach and Flinders Beach in winter is one of the few things on this island that still empties the pub. The beach is also a road with a tide window, a permit, a speed limit and shorebirds on it.

season_bias.note: The mullet run runs May to August and tailor are strong in August.

also_requires.note: Above that the gutters close out and nobody goes.
A westerly off the land. Clean and cold.

cast.why: Reads the gutter, not the forecast, and is the reason the word goes around.
Has a spot, has had it for thirty years, and is about to have company.
Saw four vehicles turn off and followed them.
Watching the tide window, the speed and the roost at the north end.
Allowed to stay up for it, which is the whole point.

beats.name: A cold clear morning
beats.what_happens: A westerly, a clean sea, and the first person down there before light comes back with a bag.
beats.legible: The wind direction and the tailor index are both readable in the ecology and weather panels.
beats.chronicle: It was cold and westerly and the first bloke down there came back with eight.

beats.name: Word goes around
beats.what_happens: By mid afternoon it is on the club board, in the shop and in three phone calls. Everyone knows exactly which gutter.
beats.legible: Beach vehicle counts climb through the afternoon on the traffic layer.
beats.chronicle: By four it was on the board at the club and everyone knew which gutter.

beats.name: The tide window
beats.what_happens: The permit rule is no driving within two hours either side of high tide. High is at nine. The fish are on at seven. Somebody is going to be on the beach when they should not be.
beats.legible: A tide window bar showing when the beach is legally driveable, with the fishing window overlaid.
beats.chronicle: High tide was at nine and the fish were on at seven.

beats.name: Somebody gets stuck
beats.what_happens: One vehicle stays too long. Soft sand, a rising tide, and four other vehicles stop to help, which is what happens and is also why a small problem takes six people.
beats.legible: A vehicle stops moving on the beach route and other vehicles converge on it.
beats.chronicle: One got bogged near the north end and four utes stopped, which is more help than anyone needed.

beats.name: Fish in the freezer
beats.what_happens: Three households eat fish for a week and two more get a bag left on the step. The roost at the north end had a bad night and nobody counts that.
beats.legible: Household food stores rise, and shorebird disturbance rises at the same time in a different panel.
beats.chronicle: There were bags of fish on three front steps by Sunday and the roost at the north end was down two hundred birds.

branches.question: Does anyone hold the tide window?

options.label: Everyone comes off in time
options.cost: You leave while they are still biting.

options.label: One vehicle stays
options.cost: A bogging, a tow, and possibly a rescue.

options.label: Half of them stay
options.cost: Track damage, a compliance response, and pressure on the seasonal closure lever.

well.label: A good week
well.conditions: No incident and the run holds for more than three days.
changes: a rare unambiguously good chronicle entry
well.chronicle: It went for five days and everybody got some.

badly.label: The north end pays
badly.conditions: Significant roost disturbance or a vehicle incident requiring a rescue.
badly.chronicle: The birds moved off the north end and did not come back that season.

quietly.label: It went off
quietly.conditions: Default. The wind swung and the run stopped after two days.
quietly.chronicle: The wind swung nor east on Wednesday and that was the end of it.

seeds.source: data/ecology.json seasonal_calendar winter entries: the mullet run May to August, tailor in the gutters strong in August; data/transport.json beach_driving permit rules, Main Beach 60 km/h, Flinders Beach 40 km/h, no driving two hours either side of high tide, 4WD only; data/businesses.json point-lookout-fishing-club.
seeds.notes: The tide window is published three different ways by three different sources. This seed uses the two hour rule from Minjerribah Camping, which issues and enforces the permit, and the transport pack records the conflict. The fishing club is real and incorporated but publishes no competition calendar, so no competition is named here.

seeds.title: The last boat goes
