seeds.one_line: A student on the mainland misses the afternoon water taxi by four minutes and there is not another one that gets them home.
seeds.of_this_place: The island has a primary school and no high school. Every secondary student crosses the bay twice a day on a walk-on boat with a student travel pass, and the timetable is the whole day. Missing it is not a late train.

cast.why: Fifteen, on the mainland, with a phone at eight per cent.
On the island, at work, with a car that cannot get across.
Catches the same boats and knows about a later one, or knows somebody.
Ran the boat, saw them running down the ramp, and could not hold it.
Has a relative on the mainland side and offers a couch before anyone asks.

beats.name: The usual crossing
beats.what_happens: The student does the crossing they do every day: bus, boat, bus. It is about two hours each way and it is completely normal to them.
beats.legible: The agent has a fixed daily route across the bay.
beats.chronicle: They did the crossing the way they do every day.

beats.name: Four minutes
beats.what_happens: A bus is late on the mainland side, or a class runs over. The boat goes. The next one is not soon enough, or is the last one and is full.
beats.legible: The agent is on the wrong side of the bay with no scheduled service left.
beats.chronicle: The bus was late and the boat went without them.

beats.name: Who is on that side
beats.what_happens: Ring around for someone with a couch at Cleveland, pay for a private transfer, or get a lift with whoever is driving off the last barge.
beats.legible: Three costs: a favour, about a hundred dollars, or an hour of waiting at a terminal.
beats.chronicle: They started ringing people who might be on that side.

beats.name: Somebody drives to Cleveland
beats.what_happens: A neighbour who was on the mainland anyway changes their afternoon. Or nobody was, and the household pays for a transfer they cannot afford, or the kid sleeps at a relative's and misses a day.
beats.legible: Either a cash cost appears on the household, or a new obligation edge does.
beats.chronicle: Somebody who was over there anyway waited an hour and brought them home.

beats.name: The arrangement
beats.what_happens: The household sets up a standing arrangement with somebody. It works for about a year and then that person moves.
beats.legible: A standing relationship edge that later threads can draw on and later break.
beats.chronicle: After that there was an arrangement, which held until the other family left.

branches.question: Favour, money, or a missed day?

options.label: Someone on that side helps
options.cost: An obligation, which is the cheapest and most expensive option here.

options.label: Pay for a private transfer
options.cost: Real money out of a household that is already paying to live on an island.

options.label: Sleep on the mainland
options.cost: A missed school day and a parent who did not sleep.

well.label: Home by eight
well.conditions: The student is home the same night at no cash cost.
well.chronicle: They were home by eight and somebody was owed a favour.

badly.label: A night on the wrong side
badly.conditions: The student does not get home.
badly.chronicle: They stayed at an aunt's at Cleveland and missed Thursday.

quietly.label: Paid for it
quietly.chronicle: They paid for a transfer and did not talk about what it cost.

seeds.source: data/transport.json structural fact school-travel-crosses-the-bay and the Translink School Travel Assistance Scheme student travel pass requirement; Redland City Bulletin, Dunwich high school closes its doors, recording the closure of the Year 8 to 10 secondary department in 2012 and the move of its six students to Cleveland District State High School (https://www.redlandcitybulletin.com.au/story/247451/dunwich-high-school-closes-its-doors/); data/residents.json drama hook, a high schooler misses the water taxi and the whole day falls apart.
seeds.notes: Real water taxi departure times are recorded in data/transport.json and were re-checked on 7 August 2026. This seed never states a specific departure time, because the two operators differ by fifteen minutes on two afternoon sailings and that gap is exactly the kind of thing a local would catch.

seeds.title: The weather holds the boats
seeds.one_line: Somebody needs a hospital that is not on this island, and everything that floats is tied up.
seeds.of_this_place: There is a small clinic, a community controlled health service and an ambulance station, and there is no hospital. When the weather stops the boats, the island's medical capacity is whatever is already standing on it, and the fallback is an aircraft into a small airfield or a helicopter onto an apron.

cast.why: Is the entire escalation path until something can fly or float.
The family member who is sitting there and cannot do anything.
Marine Rescue Queensland North Stradbroke works with the ambulance service on medical evacuations, and they are watching the same wind.
Has seen this before and is quietly organising the practical things nobody else has thought of.
Would go, and knows that going would be the wrong call.

beats.name: A blowing day
beats.what_happens: Wind over thirty knots, rain, everything shut. The island does what it does on a day like this, which is stay home.
beats.legible: All ferry services show suspended and the island is visibly quiet.
beats.chronicle: It blew thirty five all day and nothing ran.

beats.name: The call comes in
beats.what_happens: A medical job that needs more than the island has. The clinic stabilises. The transfer is the problem, not the treatment.
beats.legible: An emergency marker with a timer, and every transport option greyed out except two.
beats.chronicle: The job came in about four and there was no boat.

beats.name: Air, sea, or hold
beats.what_happens: A helicopter can come if the wind is inside limits. A rescue vessel can go if the skipper judges it. Or the patient is held on the island until morning under whatever care is here.
beats.legible: Three options with a wind limit, a sea state and a hold time next to each.
beats.chronicle: They asked for the helicopter.

beats.name: Whichever it is, somebody is awake all night
beats.what_happens: The transfer happens or it does not. Either way the same three or four people carry it, and two of them are volunteers with jobs in the morning.
beats.legible: Volunteer fatigue rises sharply and stays high for days.
beats.chronicle: It got done about two in the morning and three of them were at work by seven.

beats.name: Nobody says anything about it
beats.what_happens: It is not discussed. The people involved see each other at the shop and it does not come up. The emergency readiness number moves and nobody outside those four knows why.
beats.legible: The emergency readiness metric moves with a traceable reason in the chronicle.
beats.chronicle: It never came up again, which is how that works here.

branches.question: Does anything go?

options.label: Aircraft
options.cost: Wind limited, and the airfield has its own conditions.

options.label: A vessel goes anyway
options.cost: Puts the crew in the same weather.
effects: small chance of a second incident

options.label: Held until morning
options.cost: Hours, and the outcome is not in anybody's hands.
effects: the outcome is decided by the health system, not by this seed

well.label: Got across
well.conditions: The transfer completes within the window.
changes: strong trust edges between the responders
well.chronicle: They got across about two and the wind dropped by six.

badly.label: Waited it out
badly.conditions: No transfer before morning.
badly.chronicle: They waited it out and the boat ran at seven.

quietly.label: The wind dropped
quietly.conditions: Services resume before the transfer is needed.
quietly.chronicle: The wind came off about eight and the boat went.

seeds.source: data/transport.json emergency_transport, Marine Rescue Queensland North Stradbroke operating since 1977 from Yabbie Street with a medical evacuation role alongside the Queensland Ambulance Service; Dunwich Airfield (YDUN) operational guidelines effective 1 February 2024, including the note that helicopters are currently directed to the apron south of the passenger shelter while remedial works proceed; data/businesses.json health and emergency entries.
seeds.notes: This seed must never name a diagnosis, describe a clinical decision, or resolve a medical outcome. The outcome belongs to a health system, not to the narrative director. It is capped at one run per sim-year for that reason. The existence of a permanently staffed ambulance point at Point Lookout is unconfirmed and is not assumed anywhere in this seed.

seeds.title: The morning call
seeds.one_line: The support worker who did four morning visits leaves the island because she could not find a rental, and four households find out on a Tuesday.
seeds.of_this_place: In-home aged and disability support here is a handful of people driving between three townships. There is no depth in the roster. One person leaving is not a staffing problem, it is four people who do not get up on time.

cast.why: Loves the job, cannot afford to stay, and is the one who has to tell four people.
Gets the morning visit. It is also the only conversation some days.
A family member who will now do it, on top of a job.
Now covering visits that are not clinical work, which means clinic hours go somewhere else.
Explains why worker accommodation is a three year project.

beats.name: Quarter past seven
beats.what_happens: Four visits a morning, same order, same times. Meds, a shower, breakfast, and a conversation. It looks like nothing and it is the whole system.
beats.legible: A worker agent with a fixed daily route between four households.
beats.chronicle: Four visits a morning, same order, for two and a half years.

beats.name: The lease is not renewed
beats.what_happens: Her rental goes to short stay or sells. There is nothing to rent. The job pays what it pays and the island costs what it costs.
beats.legible: A dwelling changes use and a worker household shows housing insecurity.
beats.chronicle: The place she rented went to short stay in September.

beats.name: Is there a bed on this island
beats.what_happens: Employer accommodation, a room with one of the households she visits, which is a boundary problem, or she goes.
beats.legible: The worker beds number is visible and is either zero or not.
beats.chronicle: There were no worker beds and there was one spare room, which was not going to work.

beats.name: The visits stop
beats.what_happens: Four households lose a morning visit. Two families absorb it. One person starts missing medication. One goes to the mainland for care and does not come back.
beats.legible: Four households show an unmet care need, and health access falls.
beats.chronicle: Two families picked it up and one person went to the mainland in February.

beats.name: The job is advertised
beats.what_happens: The position is advertised. It stays open. Anyone who could do it would have the same housing problem, and everybody involved can see that.
beats.legible: The vacancy stays open with a visible reason attached to it.
beats.chronicle: The job was still advertised in June.

branches.question: Can the island house the person it needs?

options.label: A worker bed exists
options.cost: Requires the worker accommodation lever, which takes years and a budget.

options.label: She commutes from the mainland
options.cost: Two ferries a day at her own expense. It lasts about four months.

options.label: She leaves
options.cost: Four households.

well.label: She stayed
well.conditions: Housing found within the window.
well.chronicle: They found her a place at Dunwich and the visits kept going.

badly.label: Four households
badly.conditions: She leaves and the role is unfilled at 90 days.
changes: one resident leaves the island for care
badly.chronicle: The visits stopped in October and by autumn one of the four was living at Cleveland.

quietly.label: Commuting for now
quietly.chronicle: She started commuting, which everyone said would not last.

seeds.source: data/residents.json drama hook, a support worker leaves the island because they could not find a rental and four older residents lose their morning call; data/residents.json occupation aged-and-disability-support-worker and household one-mile-aged-support-household; data/civic.json worker-accommodation-build and community-housing-expansion levers.
seeds.notes: Nareeba Moopi Moopi Pa is trading-unconfirmed in the businesses pack and is referenced here as a place, not as an employer with named capacity. No care rosters, client numbers or funding arrangements for this island are published and none are asserted.

seeds.title: The bins after the weekend
seeds.one_line: Everything a long weekend brought over has to go back the same way, and it does not fit.
seeds.of_this_place: Waste on this island is a stock with a barge-limited outflow. Ten thousand extra people over three days do not take their rubbish home. It sits at the transfer station until there is a sailing with room for it.

also_requires.note: It becomes visible on the Tuesday, after they have gone.

cast.why: Is the person standing at the gate saying the site is full.
Has a trailer of green waste and has been waiting for the site to reopen for four days.
Turns over eleven houses on the Tuesday and each one produces the same three bags.
Is picking up what did not make it into a bin at all.
Left the esky. Genuinely thought somebody would want it.

beats.name: Bins out Sunday
beats.what_happens: The bins go out Sunday afternoon for a Monday collection, the way they do. Everything looks normal.
beats.legible: Bins render at the kerb and the waste stock starts rising.
beats.chronicle: The bins went out Sunday afternoon like always.

beats.name: The site is full
beats.what_happens: The transfer station is at capacity and there is no barge slot until later in the week. The gate is shut on people with trailers.
beats.legible: The waste facility shows full and a queue forms at its gate.
beats.chronicle: The transfer station was full by Tuesday and the gate stayed shut.

beats.name: Where does it go
beats.what_happens: Hold it, pay to prioritise a waste sailing over a commercial one, or let it sit at the kerb for another three days in summer.
beats.legible: The barge slot allocation is visible as a trade-off against other freight.
beats.chronicle: It came down to whether a waste sailing beat a freight one.

beats.name: Three days in February
beats.what_happens: Whatever is not moved sits. In summer that means smell, birds, and things getting into it. In any season it means the next weekend starts from behind.
beats.legible: Litter and amenity metrics move, and the next period starts with a backlog.
beats.chronicle: It sat until Friday and the following weekend started from behind.

beats.name: The esky
beats.what_happens: Somebody takes the abandoned esky home and uses it for six years. Nobody counts that either.
beats.legible: A small reuse event, which is the island-reuse-and-repair lever in miniature.
beats.chronicle: Somebody took the esky home and it is still going.

branches.question: Waste sailing or freight sailing?

options.label: Prioritise the waste sailing
options.cost: Something commercial waits, and that costs a business money.

options.label: Hold until the scheduled sailing
options.cost: Three days of full bins in whatever the weather is.

options.label: Charge commercial waste properly
options.cost: A structural fix that makes several small businesses angry.

well.label: Cleared by Thursday
well.conditions: The backlog clears before the next inbound peak.
well.chronicle: It cleared Thursday and nobody had to think about it again.

badly.label: Two weekends deep
badly.conditions: The backlog is still there when the next peak arrives.
changes: strong pressure on the transfer station lever
badly.chronicle: It was still there when the next lot arrived.

quietly.label: Sat until Friday
quietly.chronicle: It sat until Friday.

seeds.source: data/civic.json waste issue and its five levers; data/events.json bin-day and waste-transfer-rhythm, both flagged as unverified; data/transport.json structural fact no-bridge.
seeds.notes: The single largest gap behind this seed: no public data exists on island waste tonnage, barge slot allocation, removal frequency or transfer station capacity, and the bin day itself is sourced only from a holiday letting agency page. Every number here is relative to the simulation's own stock, never absolute.

seeds.title: Smoke over Goompi
seeds.one_line: The burn goes in on a still winter morning and the smoke sits over the township all day.
seeds.of_this_place: In 2013 to 2014 a single lightning strike burned about 16,800 hectares, roughly seventy per cent of the island's bushland, over just over two weeks, and more than 900 campers were evacuated. Everyone here understands why the planned burns happen. That does not help if you have asthma and the wind is not moving.

cast.why: Is on the burn, and lives three streets from where the smoke is sitting.
Has a child or a parent with a respiratory condition and got the notification at seven this morning.
Has to decide about outdoor activities and did not get told either.
Explains the notification process, which is the actual complaint.
Thinks the burn should not happen at all and is about to learn about 2013.

beats.name: A good burn day
beats.what_happens: Cool, dry, low wind, fuel at the right moisture. The window for a planned burn on this island is narrow and this is it.
beats.legible: The fire system shows a burn window open with its conditions listed.
beats.chronicle: It was the right morning for it and everyone who does this knew it.

beats.name: The smoke does not move
beats.what_happens: No wind. The plume settles into the low ground and sits over the township. It is still there at four.
beats.legible: A visible smoke layer over the township and a smoke exposure metric climbing.
beats.chronicle: There was no wind and the smoke sat over Dunwich until dark.

beats.name: Notification, not the burn
beats.what_happens: The argument that follows is about how much warning people got, not about whether burning should happen. Those are different levers and the difference matters.
beats.legible: Two distinct levers shown side by side: how much is burnt, and how people are told.
beats.chronicle: The argument was about the notice, not the burn.

beats.name: Two households and a school
beats.what_happens: Somebody with a respiratory condition has a bad night. The school keeps the kids inside. Two people who otherwise agree with each other spend a week not agreeing.
beats.legible: Household health needs and school activity both change for a day.
beats.chronicle: The school kept them inside and one household did not sleep.

beats.name: Fuel load down
beats.what_happens: The hazard load in that block drops for years. Nobody will ever notice the fire that does not happen. The volunteer who copped the complaints is at the same shop on Saturday.
beats.legible: Fire hazard load drops in that vegetation block and stays down for several sim years.
beats.chronicle: The fuel load in that block went down for about a decade and nobody will ever thank anyone for it.

branches.question: Notice, timing, or extent?

options.label: Improve notification and timing
options.cost: Cheap, slow, and it does not reduce the smoke.

options.label: Burn less
options.cost: Fire hazard load rises and stays risen.

options.label: Leave it
options.cost: The same argument next winter.

well.label: Better notice next time
well.conditions: The notification lever advances.
well.chronicle: The notification list got longer and the burns kept going.

badly.label: Less burnt
badly.conditions: Burn extent is reduced.
badly.chronicle: They burnt less that winter, which felt better at the time.

quietly.label: It cleared by morning
quietly.chronicle: A breeze came up overnight and by morning you could not smell it.

seeds.source: Redlands Coast Today, a decade on from the 2013 to 2014 fires: a single lightning strike, more than 16,800 ha and an estimated seventy per cent of the island's bushland, over just over two weeks from 29 December 2013, with nine hundred campers evacuated from Main Beach and the Blue Lake area on New Year's Day (https://www.redlandscoasttoday.com.au/2023/12/a-decade-on-from-devastating-bushfires-and-minjerribah-is-stronger-than-ever/); Queensland Reconstruction Authority record of the North Stradbroke Island fires, 29 December 2013 (https://www.qra.qld.gov.au/node/186); data/ecology.json proc-fire-regime; data/civic.json fire issue with planned-burn-extent and burn-notification-and-timing levers.
seeds.notes: Fire return intervals in the ecology pack are modelling placeholders, so this seed never states an interval. Cultural burning is documented in the ecology pack with a handling rule that it must not be rendered from that pack, and it is deliberately absent here: this seed is about a council and rural fire brigade hazard reduction burn only.

seeds.title: Bait season
seeds.one_line: The fox control program goes in around April and somebody's dog is off the lead in the wrong place.
seeds.of_this_place: The coordinated fox program on this island is the clearest ecological win anyone has had here: about ninety per cent of foxes removed and no recorded turtle nest predation since late 2016. It is also a recurrent budget line and it puts bait in country where people walk dogs.

season_bias.note: Fox control season begins about April.

cast.why: Did not see the sign, or saw it and did not know what it meant.
Put the signs up, runs the program, and has to have this conversation every autumn.
Remembers foxes taking turtle nests and has no patience left for this argument.
Would rather nobody's dog died and also knows what the program is for.
Walks the same tracks and has the map in their head.

beats.name: Signs go up
beats.what_happens: The program starts. Signs at the track heads, a notice, the same as last year.
beats.legible: Baiting areas render on the map with a season and a boundary.
beats.chronicle: The signs went up at the track heads in the first week of April.

beats.name: A dog off the lead
beats.what_happens: Somebody walks in from a track that does not have a sign on it, or walks past the one that does. Nothing happens for four days and then something nearly does.
beats.legible: A dog agent enters a baiting polygon and a risk marker appears.
beats.chronicle: A dog got in behind the dunes on the Thursday.

beats.name: How this gets handled
beats.what_happens: Quiet word, formal complaint, or a note on the community page. The last one turns two neighbours into a hundred people with opinions.
beats.legible: Three escalation paths with a different friction cost and a different chance of the behaviour changing.
beats.chronicle: Somebody put it on the community page.

beats.name: The program is what is at stake
beats.what_happens: Enough friction and the program gets curtailed or moved, which is how a fox comes back. The people arguing about a dog are actually arguing about turtle nests and nobody says that out loud.
beats.legible: The feral control lever shows pressure, and the ecology panel shows what happens to nest predation if it lapses.
beats.chronicle: The program was the thing at stake and nobody said so.

beats.name: Nothing happened
beats.what_happens: The dog is fine. The season ends. The signs come down. Next April the same three people have the same conversation with different words.
beats.legible: Fox index stays low, nest predation stays at zero, and the player can see the connection.
beats.chronicle: Nothing happened, and the signs came down in July.

branches.question: Quiet word or public post?

options.label: A quiet word at the shop
options.cost: Awkward for one afternoon.

options.label: A formal complaint
options.cost: Council time, and it makes an enemy.

options.label: Put it online
options.cost: Everyone joins in and the program gets caught in the middle.

well.label: Sorted at the shop
well.conditions: Escalation stays informal.
well.chronicle: It got sorted at the shop and that was the end of it.

badly.label: The program gets narrowed
badly.conditions: Public escalation and the lever loses ground.
changes: a slow ecological consequence the player can trace years later
badly.chronicle: The baiting area was pulled back from the tracks the following season.

quietly.label: Signs came down in July
quietly.chronicle: The signs came down in July.

seeds.source: National Feral Cat and Fox Management Coordination project page for Minjerribah / North Stradbroke Island, recording bait stations, traps and monitoring cameras and the removal of about ninety per cent of the foxes since the project began, with sea turtle nests named as a primary reason (https://feralcatandfox.com.au/resources/minjerribah-qld/); Friends of Stradbroke Island fox eradication progress (https://fosi.org.au/blog/fox-eradication-progress/); data/ecology.json proc-feral-predator-control, which also records no turtle nest predation since late 2016 and an April season start; data/civic.json feral-and-weed-control and dog-control-enforcement levers.
seeds.notes: No dog death from baiting on this island is claimed or implied as having happened. The seed is about the friction the program creates, and its worst ending is ecological, not canine. Baiting methods, bait types and exact program boundaries are not stated because none were verified.

seeds.title: A nest and a wheel track
seeds.one_line: A loggerhead comes up on Main Beach in the middle of the summer season and lays about forty metres from where everybody drives.
seeds.of_this_place: Loggerheads nest on these ocean beaches from about late October, and Main Beach is a gazetted vehicle route with a 60 km/h limit and a tide window. Both of those things are true at the same time and both have been true for decades.

cast.why: Finds the crawl at first light and has to decide what to mark and how visibly.
Camped forty metres away and would absolutely have helped if anybody had told them.
Has driven this beach since before the permits and does not need a sign to know where to drive.
Wants the whole stretch closed and knows that will not happen.
Comes down every morning for eight weeks to see whether anything has happened.

beats.name: The beach as a road
beats.what_happens: Summer on Main Beach: vehicles running the hard sand inside the tide window, camps set back off the dune, a lot of people having a good time.
beats.legible: Vehicle traffic renders on the beach route with the tide window bar showing.
beats.chronicle: There were about sixty vehicles on the beach that day.

beats.name: A crawl above the high water mark
beats.what_happens: A track up the sand and back down again, and a disturbed patch between. It is a nest and it is inside the width people drive on at the top of the tide.
beats.legible: A nest marker with an incubation countdown appears on the beach.
beats.chronicle: There was a crawl up past the high water mark and a nest at the top of it.

beats.name: Mark it or not
beats.what_happens: A marked nest gets protected and also gets visited. An unmarked nest gets driven over. There is no option where nothing has a cost.
beats.legible: Two risks quantified: interference risk if marked, crushing risk if not.
beats.chronicle: They marked it, which meant everyone knew where it was.

beats.name: Eight weeks
beats.what_happens: The nest sits for about two months through the busiest part of the year. Every big tide, every vehicle, every dog and every curious person is a chance for it to fail.
beats.legible: The nest has a visible survival probability that responds to traffic, tides and disturbance.
beats.chronicle: It sat there through January with the biggest tides of the summer over it.

beats.name: Whatever comes out of it
beats.what_happens: It hatches, or it does not, and either way about four people were watching. If it hatches, the camper who nearly parked on it tells that story for the rest of their life.
beats.legible: A hatching event or a failure event, recorded in the ecology panel with the cause.
beats.chronicle: It went off about ten one night in February with six people standing there.

branches.question: Mark it, move it, or close the stretch?

options.label: Mark and monitor
options.cost: Draws people to it.

options.label: Close that section of beach to vehicles
options.cost: Cuts the beach route in the peak season and makes a lot of people angry.

options.label: Leave it unmarked
options.cost: It is on a road.

well.label: It hatched
well.conditions: The nest survives to hatching.
changes: the camper becomes a repeat visitor
well.chronicle: It went off in February and everybody who was there still talks about it.

badly.label: Wheel tracks over it
badly.conditions: The nest fails to vehicle or tide damage.
badly.chronicle: There were tracks across it after the January long weekend.

quietly.label: Washed out
quietly.conditions: A spring tide takes it and nobody is to blame.
quietly.chronicle: The big tide in January went right over it.

seeds.source: data/ecology.json seasonal_calendar, loggerhead turtle nesting and hatching on the ocean beaches in summer and loggerhead mating from late October; data/transport.json beach_driving rules, Main Beach 60 km/h, 4WD only, no driving two hours either side of high tide; data/civic.json beach-driving-seasonal-closures lever.
seeds.notes: No nest count, hatching success rate or monitoring program for this island was verified. The nest survival probability must be computed by the ecology system, not asserted here. The fox program note in data/ecology.json records no turtle nest predation since late 2016, which is a separate matter from vehicle risk.

seeds.title: The power goes
seeds.one_line: The island loses power on a hot afternoon and the first thing anyone thinks about is the freezers.
seeds.of_this_place: Power comes to this island across the bay. When it stops, there is no other island grid to fall back on, and every business here holds a week of stock in a freezer because the next delivery is a boat away.

cast.why: Has about four thousand dollars of stock and a generator that may or may not start.
Somebody in the house is on equipment that needs mains power.
Has the only decent generator on the street and is about to spend the afternoon moving it.
Doing the ring around, which is the actual emergency system on an island this size.
Cannot pay for anything, because nobody's card machine works.

beats.name: A hot Thursday
beats.what_happens: Thirty two degrees, everything running, the shops full, the pumps going.
beats.legible: Normal economic activity across all three townships.
beats.chronicle: It was thirty two and everything was going.

beats.name: Everything stops at once
beats.what_happens: Power out island-wide. No pumps, no card machines, no freezers, no phones once the towers run their batteries down.
beats.legible: Businesses show closed, fuel becomes unavailable, and a countdown starts on refrigerated stock.
beats.chronicle: The power went about two and the card machines went with it.

beats.name: Whose generator goes where
beats.what_happens: There are a handful of working generators on the island. They can go to a shop, to a household on equipment, or to the aged care place. They cannot go to all three.
beats.legible: A visible allocation with three claimants and not enough generators.
beats.chronicle: There were four generators worth having and three places that needed one.

beats.name: What spoils
beats.what_happens: Whatever does not get a generator loses stock, or gets moved, or gets by. The shop that loses a freezer wears it, because insurance on this island is its own conversation.
beats.legible: A business takes a real financial hit that is visible in its viability.
beats.chronicle: The shop lost most of a freezer and did not claim it.

beats.name: The barbecue
beats.what_happens: Somebody cooks what was going to spoil anyway, on a barbecue, in the street, and about forty people eat. That is not a heartwarming detail, it is the cheapest way to deal with a freezer full of meat.
beats.legible: A social gathering event with unusually high attendance and cross-township mixing.
beats.chronicle: They cooked the lot on the barbecue out the front and about forty people ate.

branches.question: Who gets the generators?

options.label: Households on equipment first
options.cost: Two businesses lose stock.

options.label: The shops, so there is food tomorrow
options.cost: A household has to be moved to the clinic.
effects: a household displaced for a night

options.label: Nobody decides and it sorts itself out
options.cost: It mostly works and one thing falls through.
effects: random allocation weighted by existing relationships, which is realistic and unfair

well.label: Nobody lost much
well.conditions: Outage under six hours and equipment households covered.
changes: trust edges up across the township
well.chronicle: It came back about eight and the only casualty was a freezer full of prawns.

badly.label: Two days
badly.conditions: Outage over 24 hours.
badly.chronicle: It was two days and half the fridges on the island got emptied into a skip.

quietly.label: Back before dark
quietly.chronicle: It was back before dark.

seeds.source: General reasoning from data/transport.json structural fact no-bridge and data/businesses.json stock-holding businesses. No island power supply arrangement, outage history, generator inventory or backup capacity was verified.
seeds.notes: This is the least evidenced seed in the pack and it is marked low for that reason. Nothing is claimed about how power reaches this island, because nothing was verified. The seed fires purely on the simulation's own outage state. If the infrastructure pack establishes the real arrangement, rewrite the of_this_place line first.

seeds.title: A main in January
seeds.one_line: A water main goes at Point Lookout on the second of January with the township at four times its normal population.
seeds.of_this_place: This island sits on a sand aquifer that supplies its own townships and exports water to the mainland grid. Having water underneath you is not the same as having water in the pipe, and the pipe was sized for the people who live here.

cast.why: Called in on the second of January, which is not what anybody planned.
Has eleven houses full of people who all want a shower at the same time.
Paid a lot for this week and is being reasonable about it, which somehow makes it worse.
Has a rainwater tank and thinks everyone should.
Cannot open the kitchen without water and is now not being paid.

beats.name: Peak
beats.what_happens: The township at its absolute fullest. Every house occupied, campgrounds full, the shop out of half of everything by eleven.
beats.legible: Township population multiple visible in the crowd panel.
beats.chronicle: Point Lookout was about four times its usual size.

beats.name: The pressure drops
beats.what_happens: A main goes. Pressure falls across a chunk of the township. Toilets, showers, kitchens, and one surf club with a full car park.
beats.legible: Water pressure by township, with the affected area shaded.
beats.chronicle: A main went about six in the morning and half the township had no pressure by eight.

beats.name: Fix it now or fix it properly
beats.what_happens: A patch today with a crew who are on the island, or a proper repair that needs plant brought over on the barge and takes three days.
beats.legible: Two repair paths with a duration and a failure probability each.
beats.chronicle: They patched it, because the plant to do it properly was two days away on the barge.

beats.name: Everything downstream
beats.what_happens: No water means no kitchen, no toilets at the beach, and campgrounds with three hundred people and nowhere to wash. It becomes a public health question inside a day.
beats.legible: Businesses close, campground amenities go offline, and the visitor satisfaction metric drops.
beats.chronicle: Three kitchens shut and the campground amenities went off at lunchtime.

beats.name: The tank
beats.what_happens: Two households with rainwater tanks run a hose out the front. Somebody puts a note up about it. Half the street asks what a tank costs and none of them get one.
beats.legible: A small resilience behaviour that the player can later make into a policy.
beats.chronicle: Two houses ran a hose out the front and that got most of the street through.

branches.question: Patch or proper?

options.label: Patch it today
options.cost: It will go again, probably next summer.
effects: the seed becomes more likely next peak

options.label: Bring the plant over
options.cost: Three days without water in the busiest week of the year.

options.label: Truck water in and patch later
options.cost: Barge slots, and the trucks compete with everything else on a full road.

well.label: Water by evening
well.conditions: Supply restored within twelve hours.
changes: a good story about the hose
well.chronicle: It was back by evening and the pub did a very good night.

badly.label: Three days
badly.conditions: Supply out for more than 48 hours in peak.
badly.chronicle: It took three days and about a third of the campground went home early.

quietly.label: Patched by lunch
quietly.chronicle: They had it patched by lunch and said they would do it properly in the winter.

seeds.source: data/ecology.json proc-groundwater: island township extraction of about 1.6 ML per day and export to the south-east Queensland grid, all marked low confidence in that pack; data/civic.json water-and-wastewater and water-security issues and their metrics.
seeds.notes: Every water volume figure available for this island is secondary reporting and one figure in the same source was garbled, so no volume is stated here. The seed uses a pressure index, which is the simulation's own. Whether Point Lookout is reticulated the way this seed assumes was not verified.

seeds.title: No booking until Thursday
seeds.one_line: A builder needs a truck of frames on the island by Monday and the first vehicle booking is Thursday.
seeds.of_this_place: Every sheet of ply, every roof truss and every bag of cement on this island came over on a vehicle sailing that somebody booked. In the peak the barge is sold out days ahead and a trade job is not a priority over a family in a Prado.

cast.why: Has a crew booked, a crane day booked and a slab that needs to be covered before the weather.
It is their build, and they are paying for the delay without understanding it.
Also cannot get a booking, for an entirely different and equally reasonable reason.
Has an opinion about resident priority booking that they are not allowed to express at work.
Loads the boat, and can see exactly how much of it is one family's camper trailer.

beats.name: A crew and a crane day
beats.what_happens: A small build with a tight sequence: materials Monday, crew Tuesday, crane Wednesday, roof on before the weekend.
beats.legible: A construction job with a visible dependency chain.
beats.chronicle: The frames were meant to be on the island Monday.

beats.name: Sold out
beats.what_happens: Every vehicle sailing to Thursday is booked. The waitlist is a standby queue at Toondah with a success rate nobody publishes.
beats.legible: The barge booking availability is visible and is genuinely full.
beats.chronicle: Every sailing was booked to Thursday and standby was a queue with no promises.

beats.name: Standby, split, or stand down
beats.what_happens: Sit on standby at Toondah and hope, split the load into things that can go as walk-on freight on the passenger boat, or stand the crew down and pay them anyway or not.
beats.legible: Three costs with different people bearing them: fuel and hours, a fiddly split load, or a crew's week.
beats.chronicle: He sat on standby from five in the morning.

beats.name: Somebody is not paid
beats.what_happens: A stood-down crew is a stood-down week for two or three households. If they are mainland based they go and work somewhere else and the next job here is harder to staff.
beats.legible: Household income drops for the affected agents and the job's completion date slips.
beats.chronicle: The crew lost three days and two of them took work on the mainland after that.

beats.name: It costs more
beats.what_happens: The build costs more than the quote, which is what everyone on this island already knew and could not prove. The freight index moves and every other build in the sim gets slightly harder.
beats.legible: The freight cost index moves and shows up in the cost of every construction job.
beats.chronicle: It cost about nine per cent more than the quote and the quote had allowed for that.

branches.question: Who gets priority on a full boat?

options.label: Priority booking for residents and trades
options.cost: Visitors get bumped, which is the visitor economy.

options.label: More peak sailings
options.cost: Money, crew, and more traffic on East Coast Road.

options.label: Nothing changes
options.cost: Everyone builds it into their price, permanently.

well.label: Got on standby
well.conditions: The load crosses within two days of the target.
changes: obligation edge to whoever at the ramp made room
well.chronicle: He got on the second standby and the roof went on Friday.

badly.label: Stood down
badly.conditions: The load misses by more than four days.
changes: a mainland crew stops taking island work
badly.chronicle: The crew went and worked at Capalaba and the slab sat open through the rain.

quietly.label: Rebooked for Thursday
quietly.chronicle: They rebooked for Thursday and everything moved a week.

seeds.source: data/transport.json SeaLink SEQ terms and conditions, including the 20 minute vehicle check-in cut, the two hour online change cut, the A$10 cancellation fee and the 100 per cent no-show forfeit; structural facts busiest-days and walk-on-freight-rides-the-passenger-boat; data/civic.json barge-queue issue and its levers.
seeds.notes: The walk-on freight split in the choice beat is real and counterintuitive: on this route walk-on freight goes on the passenger ferry, may travel unaccompanied and is charged per item. That is from the operator terms and is one of the more useful facts in the transport pack. The standby success rate is modelled and flagged in that pack.

seeds.title: The flat battery off Amity
seeds.one_line: A tinnie goes quiet on the run home with the tide going out through Rainbow Channel, and somebody's Sunday afternoon becomes a callout.
seeds.of_this_place: Marine Rescue Queensland North Stradbroke has been operating from Yabbie Street overlooking One Mile since 1977, crewed by volunteers. The water between Amity and Moreton is a real channel with real tide, and most callouts are not dramatic, they are a flat battery and a long tow.

also_requires.note: Within three hours of dark, which is when it stops being a nuisance and starts being a job.

cast.why: Was about to have dinner. Goes anyway. Has done about two hundred of these.
Hired or trailered a boat, did everything roughly right, and got unlucky.
Was on the water, heard it on the radio, and gets there first because that is how this works.
Watching from the ramp, calling it, and has opinions about the anchor.
At home with the volunteer's dinner going cold, again.

beats.name: A good afternoon on the water
beats.what_happens: Boats out off Amity on the run out, a light nor easter, twenty or thirty tinnies between the point and the banks.
beats.legible: Small vessels render on the water with the tide direction visible.
beats.chronicle: There were about thirty boats out off Amity.

beats.name: It will not start
beats.what_happens: One boat stops. The tide is taking it the wrong way. It is two hours to dark and the radio call is calm, which is worse than if it was not.
beats.legible: A drifting vessel marker with a projected track and a countdown to sunset.
beats.chronicle: One of them called in at about four with no motor and the tide taking them out.

beats.name: Who goes
beats.what_happens: The volunteer crew, a nearby private boat, or both. A private tow is faster and has no insurance and no protocol behind it.
beats.legible: Response time for each option and the risk attached to each.
beats.chronicle: Someone who was already out there got there first.

beats.name: The long tow
beats.what_happens: A tow back against the tide is slow. Two or three hours of somebody's evening. The crew are back on the water again next Sunday and the Sunday after.
beats.legible: Volunteer hours accumulate, and the volunteer roster shows who has done how many.
beats.chronicle: The tow took two and a half hours against the tide and they got in after dark.

beats.name: A donation and a beer
beats.what_happens: The person who got towed makes a donation, or does not. They tell the story at the club. Somebody points out that the volunteer crew is nine people for the whole island.
beats.legible: A small donation event, and the volunteer roster depth becomes visible to the player.
beats.chronicle: He put a hundred in the tin and told the story at the club, which is about the going rate.

branches.question: Volunteer crew or the nearest boat?

options.label: The volunteer crew goes
options.cost: Fuel, hours, and four people's evening.

options.label: A private boat tows them
options.cost: Faster, and if it goes wrong there is nothing behind it.
effects: small chance of a second incident

options.label: They anchor and wait for the tide
options.cost: A night on the water, which is only sometimes the wrong call.

well.label: In before eight
well.conditions: The vessel is recovered before dark or shortly after.
well.chronicle: They were on the trailer by eight and the crew went home.

badly.label: Out all night
badly.conditions: Weather turns during the response or a second incident occurs.
badly.chronicle: It turned into an all-night job and two of the crew missed work.

quietly.label: Someone gave them a tow
quietly.chronicle: Somebody who was out there anyway gave them a tow in.

seeds.source: data/transport.json emergency_transport: Marine Rescue Queensland North Stradbroke, base at Yabbie Street overlooking One Mile, operating since 1977, with its operating area and the medical evacuation role alongside the Queensland Ambulance Service; data/places.json amity-boat-ramp and polka-point.
seeds.notes: Crew numbers, callout volumes, vessel details and response times for the unit are not published and none are stated. The nine-person figure in the coda beat is written as something a character notices, not as a fact, and the director should render it from the simulation's own roster rather than as a constant.

seeds.title: The roost at the north end
seeds.one_line: A dog runs a roosting flock off the flats twice in a week, and the birds do not come back.
seeds.of_this_place: The western flats here hold migratory shorebirds that fly to the northern hemisphere and back. Eastern curlew and bar-tailed godwit are both listed as critically endangered. Being flushed off a roost is not a scare, it is a fuel cost on a bird that has to cross the Pacific.

season_bias.note: Peak numbers in summer, departing about April, returning from about September.

also_requires.note: High tide roosting, which is when they are packed onto the last dry sand and easiest to disturb.

cast.why: Counts the roost at high tide once a month and has the numbers going back years.
Walks the dog on the flats because it is the best place on the island to walk a dog, which is exactly the problem.
Can put up a sign and cannot be there at every high tide.
Remembers when there were more of them and is not sure whether that is true or just how memory works.
Holds the off lead review and knows exactly how unpopular the answer is.

beats.name: The high tide count
beats.what_happens: A roost on the last dry sand at the top of the tide. A few hundred birds, packed in, not doing anything.
beats.legible: A roost with a count that responds to tide height.
beats.chronicle: There were about four hundred on the sand at the top of the tide.

beats.name: Up twice in a week
beats.what_happens: They get put up. Not maliciously, just a dog doing what a dog does. Then it happens again four days later.
beats.legible: A flush event animates and the roost count drops on the next survey.
beats.chronicle: They went up on the Tuesday and again on the Saturday.

beats.name: Sign, fence, or review
beats.what_happens: A sign that people read, a seasonal fence that people resent, or a formal off lead area review that takes eighteen months and makes everybody argue.
beats.legible: Three interventions with a cost, a lead time and an effectiveness estimate.
beats.chronicle: They put a sign up first, because that is what you do first.

beats.name: They move somewhere worse
beats.what_happens: The flock relocates to a roost with less feeding nearby, or spends more of the tide cycle flying. Neither shows up as a dead bird. It shows up as a smaller count next spring.
beats.legible: The roost count at this site falls and another site rises by less than the difference.
beats.chronicle: They moved down the flats to a worse spot and the count did not add back up.

beats.name: A number in a spreadsheet
beats.what_happens: The count goes in the spreadsheet. In eight years somebody uses it in a submission. That is the entire mechanism by which anything is ever proved here.
beats.legible: The player gains access to a multi-year roost count series.
beats.chronicle: It went in the spreadsheet with the other nineteen years.

branches.question: How hard do you protect a roost?

options.label: Signage
options.cost: Cheap, and about a third effective.

options.label: Seasonal roost fencing
options.cost: Materials, volunteer hours, and it looks like a lock-out.

options.label: Formal off lead area review
options.cost: Eighteen months and a very loud consultation.
effects: consultation_trust +0.03 if done properly, -0.10 if not

options.label: Nothing
options.cost: A number that gets smaller.

well.label: Fenced for the season
well.conditions: An intervention is in place before the next season.
well.chronicle: They fenced the top of the sand for the season and the count held.

badly.label: A smaller number
badly.conditions: No intervention and the count falls two seasons running.
badly.chronicle: The count was down again the next spring and nobody could say exactly why.

quietly.label: A sign went up
quietly.chronicle: A sign went up and it helped a bit.

seeds.source: data/ecology.json proc-shorebird-disturbance and the species records for eastern curlew and bar-tailed godwit, both critically endangered, with the note that their published counts are Moreton Bay totals and not island numbers; data/civic.json dog-control-enforcement and off-lead-area-review levers.
seeds.notes: No island roost count exists in public. Every count in this seed must come from the simulation's own shorebird system. The bay-wide figures in the ecology pack (eastern curlew 2,304, bar-tailed godwit 12,134) must never be displayed as island numbers, and this seed does not use them.

seeds.title: The house next door is let
seeds.one_line: The place beside a shift worker who starts at five becomes a six bedroom holiday let, and the argument is never about noise, it is about who the street is for.
seeds.of_this_place: On this island the argument about short stay letting is not abstract. It is a specific fence between a household that works here and a house that is full of different people every three days and empty the rest of the time.

cast.why: Starts at five, finishes at three, and the house next door does not sleep on the same schedule as a person with a job.
Is the only contactable human, lives on the island, and is friends with both sides.
Lives in Brisbane, is not a bad person, and is contactable only by email.
Paid nine hundred a night and is on holiday, which is a real thing to be.
Cannot enforce something that is not registered.

beats.name: The changeover
beats.what_happens: Friday afternoon on a street where four of the eight houses change over on the same day. Cars, cleaners, wheelie bins, keys in a box on the fence.
beats.legible: A visible weekly turnover pattern on the street, distinct from the resident pattern.
beats.chronicle: Four of the eight houses on that street changed over on the Friday.

beats.name: Three nights
beats.what_happens: One group is loud for three nights in a row. It is not extreme. It is enough that somebody who starts at five stops sleeping.
beats.legible: A household's sleep need goes unmet and their work performance drops.
beats.chronicle: By Sunday she had not slept properly since Thursday.

beats.name: Who do you even ring
beats.what_happens: Go over and say something, ring the letting manager who is a friend, or complain to a council that has no register and therefore no enforcement handle.
beats.legible: The absence of a register is legible as a missing enforcement path.
beats.chronicle: There was nobody to ring who could actually do anything.

beats.name: It costs a friendship
beats.what_happens: Whichever way it goes, the person who lives here and the person who manages the letting are on opposite sides of it, and they are the two people who both actually live on the island.
beats.legible: Friction rises between two resident households while the owner is unaffected.
beats.chronicle: The two people it came between were the only two who lived there.

beats.name: The next lot are lovely
beats.what_happens: The next group is quiet and delightful and stays a week. Nothing is resolved and everybody feels slightly stupid about the whole thing.
beats.legible: The pattern continues with variation, so the player sees it is structural rather than personal.
beats.chronicle: The next lot were lovely, which somehow made it worse.

branches.question: Register, cap, or nothing?

options.label: Register every short stay letting
options.cost: Administrative cost, and it makes owners feel policed.

options.label: Cap short stay by township
options.cost: The largest single intervention available in the housing issue, and the angriest.

options.label: Nothing
options.cost: The household eventually moves, which is how a street becomes entirely short stay.
effects: a resident household leaves within two years

well.label: Somebody has a number to ring
well.conditions: A registration or contact requirement is in place.
well.chronicle: After the register came in there was at least a number to ring.

badly.label: She moved
badly.conditions: The resident household relocates or leaves.
badly.chronicle: She moved to Dunwich in the winter and the house she left went on the same site.

quietly.label: It went quiet
quietly.chronicle: It went quiet after the school holidays, the way it does.

seeds.source: data/civic.json housing issue with short-stay-letting-registration, short-stay-cap-by-township and rates-differential-unoccupied levers; data/residents.json household archetypes with tenure not_a_residence; Queensland government investigation into short-term letting and housing supply, and more than 295 North Stradbroke Island short-term rentals listed on one platform alone.
seeds.notes: No island short stay registration data exists, and the platform listing count is one platform on one date. The seed fires on the simulation's own short stay share. The holiday owner is deliberately written as reasonable, because on this island most of them are, and the interesting version of this argument is between two people who both live here.

seeds.title: The boardwalk comes out
seeds.one_line: The engineers say a section of the Gorge Walk has to be rebuilt, and the only sensible time to do it is the only time the businesses make money.
seeds.of_this_place: The Gorge Walk is the free thing that everyone comes for, and it is a timber structure with foundations in rock on an exposed headland. It has been closed for repair before after rain washed out foundations on the southern side of the north gorge.

cast.why: Has an engineering report, a budget, and a room that does not want to hear either.
Winter trade is whale watchers walking that loop. Close it in winter and there is no winter.
Thinks a shorter walk with fewer people on it would not be the worst thing.
Has run a project before and offers to help, which is either useful or the most annoying thing that could happen.
Will do the work, and every load of timber and every piece of plant comes over on the barge.

beats.name: Four hundred a day
beats.what_happens: The walk carries a steady stream all day, every day, for free. It is the single most used piece of public infrastructure on the island.
beats.legible: Continuous foot traffic on the walk, visible as the highest crowd count on the island.
beats.chronicle: There were four hundred people on the walk before lunch, the way there always is.

beats.name: The report
beats.what_happens: Rain gets under a section and the report says a stretch needs new foundations into rock. That is plant, closure and months, not a working bee.
beats.legible: A closure with an engineering scope, a cost and a duration.
beats.chronicle: The report said a twenty five metre stretch needed new foundations into the rock.

beats.name: When
beats.what_happens: Do it in winter and lose the whale trade. Do it in summer and lose more visitors but not the ones the businesses depend on. Do it in stages and it takes two years and costs more.
beats.legible: Three schedules with a cost, a duration and a business impact each.
beats.chronicle: The argument was about when, not whether.

beats.name: Somebody has a bad season
beats.what_happens: Whichever window is chosen, a set of businesses wears it, and it is a different set each time. The chamber writes a letter. The letter does not change the engineering.
beats.legible: A specific set of businesses shows a viability dip tied to the closure window.
beats.chronicle: They did it through July and three places had their worst winter in years.

beats.name: It opens again
beats.what_happens: It reopens. It is better. Within a fortnight nobody remembers it was shut, including the people who wrote the letters.
beats.legible: The walk's condition value resets to full and visitor numbers recover within a month.
beats.chronicle: It opened in September and by October nobody mentioned it.

branches.question: Whose season pays for the repair?

options.label: Winter closure
options.cost: The whale watching businesses wear it.

options.label: Summer closure
options.cost: More people affected, but they came for the beach.
effects: higher works cost from crowd management

options.label: Staged over two years
options.cost: Roughly forty per cent more, and two years of half a walk.
effects: a low grade grievance that lasts two years

well.label: Open by spring
well.conditions: Works complete inside the planned window.
well.chronicle: It opened in September and it was better than it was.

badly.label: Two winters
badly.conditions: Works overrun by more than one season.
badly.chronicle: It was shut for two winters and one of the cafes did not reopen.

quietly.label: Patched and deferred
quietly.conditions: Default. A temporary fix and the real job goes into next year's budget.
changes: the seed becomes more likely next year
quietly.chronicle: They patched it and put the real job in next year's budget.

seeds.source: Redland City Bulletin, section of the Gorge Walk closed after erosion, with heavy rain before Easter washing out around boardwalk foundations on the south side of North Gorge (https://www.redlandcitybulletin.com.au/story/7225935/gorge-walk-section-closed-after-erosion/); Redlands Coast Today, analysis confirming a 25 metre section requiring reconstruction with new foundations into the underlying rock (https://news.redland.qld.gov.au/2021/06/point-lookout-gorge-walk-update-still-great-viewing/).
seeds.notes: The twenty five metre figure and the rock foundations detail are from the council's own 2021 update and are the strongest single sourced detail in this seed. The four hundred people a day figure in beat one is a story number, not a count: no visitor count for the walk is published and the director should render the simulation's own crowd number instead.

seeds.title: The beach goes and comes back
seeds.one_line: A southerly cuts a scarp into the front of Home Beach in one night, and the argument about whether to push the sand back starts in the morning.
seeds.of_this_place: An exposed east coast sandy beach loses sand in storms and gets it back over months. The people who have been here longest know that. The people whose stairs are now hanging over a two metre drop know it too and it does not help.

cast.why: Has photographs of this exact beach with no sand on it in 1974, and nobody wants to see them.
Their beach stairs now end in mid air.
Planted the dune in front of it and would like everyone to leave it alone for eighteen months.
Fields eleven calls asking when the sand is being put back.
The scarp changes where a rip sets up, which is a next-summer problem.

beats.name: A full beach
beats.what_happens: The beach at its widest, the dune vegetated, the access tracks where they have been for years.
beats.legible: Beach width and dune condition both high.
beats.chronicle: The beach was as wide as it gets in March.

beats.name: One night
beats.what_happens: A southerly with swell on a spring tide takes a big volume off the front in about ten hours and leaves a vertical face.
beats.legible: The beach profile visibly changes and a scarp renders along the front.
beats.chronicle: It took the front of the beach out in a night and left a face you could not walk up.

beats.name: Push it back or wait
beats.what_happens: Machinery on the beach now, which feels like action and mostly moves sand that was going to come back anyway, or fencing and eighteen months of patience.
beats.legible: The recovery curve is shown with and without intervention, and they mostly converge.
beats.chronicle: The choice was machinery now or fencing and eighteen months.

beats.name: The access tracks
beats.what_happens: People make new tracks over the scarp wherever it is lowest, which is exactly where the dune is weakest, and that does more damage than the storm did.
beats.legible: Informal access tracks appear on the map and dune condition falls further after the storm than during it.
beats.chronicle: Within a week there were five new tracks cut through the dune and none of them were there before.

beats.name: By next autumn
beats.what_happens: The sand comes back, mostly, over about a year. The dune plants do not, in the places where the tracks are. Somebody takes a photograph from the same spot every March.
beats.legible: The player gains a beach profile history overlay showing cut and recovery cycles.
beats.chronicle: Most of it was back by the following March and the tracks were still there.

branches.question: Machinery or patience?

options.label: Reprofile with machinery
options.cost: Expensive, and it damages what is left of the dune plants.

options.label: Fence, plant, and formalise the tracks
options.cost: Eighteen months of people complaining and one unpopular fence.

options.label: Nothing
options.cost: The informal tracks become permanent.

well.label: Fenced and planted
well.conditions: Access is formalised and the dune recovers.
well.chronicle: They fenced it, put in two proper accesses and by the second summer you could not tell.

badly.label: Five tracks
badly.conditions: No intervention and informal access persists past one season.
badly.chronicle: The tracks stayed and the next storm went further in.

quietly.label: It came back
quietly.conditions: Default. The sand returns and nothing is done.
quietly.chronicle: It came back by the following autumn, the way it does.

seeds.source: data/ecology.json proc-dune-cycle; data/civic.json coast-and-dunes issue with the dune-restoration-program lever.
seeds.notes: The storm cut volume range of 20 to 80 cubic metres per metre and the six to thirty six month recovery window in the ecology pack are order-of-magnitude placeholders for an exposed east coast sandy beach, not measurements from this island. No beach survey data for these beaches was found. This seed therefore never states a volume or a recovery time in player-facing text, only a scarp height that the dunes system computes.

seeds.title: One class, two years
seeds.one_line: The school combines two year levels into one class, and about nine families work out what that means before the letter arrives.
seeds.of_this_place: There is one primary school on this island and its secondary department closed in 2012 with six students. When the primary roll drops, the consequences arrive fast: a combined class, then a teacher not replaced, and every family does the arithmetic about whether to move before anyone says anything out loud.

season_bias.note: Enrolment planning for the next school year.

cast.why: Will teach the combined class and knows exactly which four kids it will be hardest on.
Has two kids at the school and is being priced out at the same time, which is not a coincidence.
Three generations here. The grandkids being at this school is the whole point of the arrangement.
Cannot do anything about a school and can do something about housing, and nobody connects those two things in the meeting.
Went to this school. So did their kids.

beats.name: The roll
beats.what_happens: A small school running a normal year: assembly, swimming at the pool, the same buses, the same drop-off.
beats.legible: School enrolment count visible with a year-on-year trend.
beats.chronicle: The school ran the year the way it always does.

beats.name: Three families in one year
beats.what_happens: Three families leave in twelve months, all for housing. The roll drops under the threshold for a separate class in two year levels.
beats.legible: The enrolment trend crosses a visible threshold line.
beats.chronicle: Three families went in a year and the roll went under.

beats.name: Housing, not schooling
beats.what_happens: Nothing anybody on this island can do changes a class structure. What can change is whether the next family can find somewhere to live. Those are the same problem and they are handled by different people.
beats.legible: The civic panel draws the link between the housing levers and the enrolment metric explicitly.
beats.chronicle: The only lever that touched it was a housing one.

beats.name: Two more decide
beats.what_happens: Two more families start looking at the mainland, not because of the class, but because the combined class is the thing that made them think about it.
beats.legible: Households flag a relocation intention that the player can see before it happens.
beats.chronicle: Two more families started looking at Cleveland, and it was not about the class.

beats.name: It works fine
beats.what_happens: The combined class is fine. It is genuinely fine. Everyone who was worried about it is quietly embarrassed, and the roll keeps drifting anyway.
beats.legible: No measurable education outcome change, and the enrolment trend continues regardless.
beats.chronicle: The combined class was fine and the roll kept drifting.

branches.question: Does the island house its families?

options.label: Move a housing lever
options.cost: Years, budget, and a fight.
effects: enrolment stabilises over three to five years
the connection is only visible in the long run

options.label: The community finds two rentals informally
options.cost: Depends entirely on obligation edges already in the save.

options.label: Nothing
options.cost: The trend continues.
effects: the seed becomes more likely each year

well.label: Two families housed
well.conditions: Enrolment stabilises within two years.
well.chronicle: Two families got places and the roll came back up a bit the year after.

badly.label: Down again
badly.conditions: Enrolment falls a second year.
badly.chronicle: It was down again the next year and they did not replace the position.

quietly.label: A combined class
quietly.chronicle: They ran a combined class and it was fine.

seeds.source: Redland City Bulletin, Dunwich high school closes its doors (https://www.redlandcitybulletin.com.au/story/247451/dunwich-high-school-closes-its-doors/); data/civic.json school_enrolments metric and the housing levers; data/businesses.json dunwich-state-school.
seeds.notes: No current enrolment figure for Dunwich State School was verified and none is stated. Queensland class formation rules are not modelled and are not described here beyond the ordinary fact that small schools combine year levels. The seed fires on the simulation's own enrolment trend.

seeds.title: The room splits
seeds.one_line: A consultation session on the ferry terminal upgrade fills the hall, and the people who agree about everything else do not agree about this.
seeds.of_this_place: The Dunwich (Gumpi) terminal is the island's front door and it is being rebuilt with about A$41 million of Commonwealth, Queensland and Council money. Everyone here has a view about the front door, and for once there is a consultation actually open.

cast.why: Presenting something they did not design to a room that thinks they did.
Has been to eleven of these over thirty years and can name the four that led to something.
Wants the queue fixed and does not care what it looks like.
Wants people to walk past the shops, not be routed around them.
Asks the obvious question that everyone else stopped asking in 2011.

beats.name: A notice on the door
beats.what_happens: A consultation opens with a closing date. Plans on a wall in a hall, three officers, and a table with a comment form on it.
beats.legible: A consultation appears in the civic panel with a closing date and a submission count of zero.
beats.chronicle: The consultation opened in the autumn with a closing date in June.

beats.name: A full hall
beats.what_happens: More people come than anyone planned for. The room splits three ways: fix the queue, protect the township, and do not touch it at all.
beats.legible: Interest group positions render as a visible split with rough proportions.
beats.chronicle: About seventy came and the room went three ways.

beats.name: Consult or decide
beats.what_happens: Run a real process that takes longer and produces something everyone can live with, or make the decision on the engineering and wear the trust cost. Both have been done here before.
beats.legible: The consultation trust rule is shown explicitly: deciding without the consultation model costs trust even when the decision is right.
beats.chronicle: The question was whether the process was real.

beats.name: Trust is the currency
beats.what_happens: The decision lands. Whatever it is, the trust number moves more on how it was made than on what it was. That number then makes every future lever cheaper or more expensive.
beats.legible: Consultation trust visibly changes the cost and lead time of every subsequent civic lever.
beats.chronicle: The trust number moved further than the design did.

beats.name: Four years
beats.what_happens: The build takes years. Half the people in that room will have an opinion about the finished thing that has nothing to do with what they said at the meeting.
beats.legible: A long-running project marker that a much later thread can reference.
beats.chronicle: It took four years and by the end nobody remembered what they had wanted.

branches.question: Is the consultation real?

options.label: Run a real process
options.cost: Months, and the answer may not be the one you wanted.

options.label: Decide on the engineering and explain it well
options.cost: Faster, and it still costs trust.

options.label: Decide and announce
options.cost: The cheapest today and the most expensive over a decade.

well.label: Something everyone can live with
well.conditions: A real process runs to its closing date and the outcome reflects a submission.
well.chronicle: They changed two things in the plan and that was enough.

badly.label: Announced
badly.conditions: The decision is made without the consultation model.
changes: sentiment down across long-term-residents, tourism-operators and ferry-commuters
badly.chronicle: It was announced in October and the hall did not fill again for three years.

quietly.label: Eleven submissions
quietly.conditions: Default. The consultation closes with few submissions and the project proceeds as designed.
quietly.chronicle: Eleven submissions went in and the plan did not change.

seeds.source: data/transport.json projects: the Dunwich (Gumpi) terminal upgrade, with a funding split of about A$10m Commonwealth, A$30m Queensland and A$1m Council, a consultation close date of 21 June 2026, and a recorded Council position, from local news reporting; data/civic.json sim_defaults consultation_trust_rule, which states that a lever enacted without the consultation model costs an extra 0.05 of consultation trust.
seeds.notes: The funding split came from a search of state and federal pages that could not be fetched directly and is medium confidence in the transport pack. The scope, the consultation close date and the Council position are from local news that could be read. This seed states no design detail for the upgrade, because none was verified.

seeds.title: Nobody logged the hours
seeds.one_line: Somebody sets up a way to record community hours so the work is visible, and it fails, and the reason it fails is the interesting part.
seeds.of_this_place: A very large amount of what keeps this island running is unpaid and unrecorded: the tow, the lift to the boat, the meal, the working bee, the phone call. Any attempt to count it runs into the same wall, which is that people here do not report their own hours and do not want to.

conditions.note: Observed attendance against self-reported hours. The gap is the seed.

cast.why: Has run a volunteer program somewhere else, knows this data would unlock grant funding, and is completely right.
Has done about four thousand unrecorded hours and is not going to start writing them down at seventy one.
Fills in the sheet properly every time and is the only one who does.
Knows a grant application needs a number and has never been given one.
Would log the hours if there were a way that did not feel like being audited.

beats.name: A lot of work nobody counts
beats.what_happens: A month of ordinary island life: three working bees, a rescue callout, two funerals catered, a hall set up and packed down four times.
beats.legible: Observed volunteer attendance is visible in the simulation while the logged number sits near zero.
beats.chronicle: It was an ordinary month, which is to say a lot of people did a lot of things.

beats.name: The sheet
beats.what_happens: A sheet goes up. Name, date, hours. After four weeks it has eleven entries and one of them is a joke.
beats.legible: The gap between attended and logged hours is drawn as a bar the player cannot mistake.
beats.chronicle: The sheet had eleven entries after a month and one of them said Batman.

beats.name: Count differently or stop counting
beats.what_happens: Push harder on self-reporting, which annoys everybody and does not work. Count the things that leave a trace instead: money, materials, attendance at a thing with a door. Or stop, and accept that the number does not exist.
beats.legible: Three measurement designs with a coverage estimate and a friction cost each.
beats.chronicle: They stopped asking people what they had done and started counting what left a mark.

beats.name: What a number is for
beats.what_happens: With no number there is no grant. With a money-only number there is a smaller grant and it is defensible. With a made-up number there is a grant and an acquittal problem in three years.
beats.legible: A funding application succeeds or fails with the evidence quality shown.
beats.chronicle: The application went in with the money figure and no hours, and it got about half.

beats.name: The same eleven people
beats.what_happens: The work carries on exactly as before, done by roughly the same eleven people, uncounted. The only thing that changed is that one person now knows why it cannot be counted.
beats.legible: The volunteer load concentration is now visible to the player as a named risk.
beats.chronicle: The same eleven people kept doing it and nobody wrote any of it down.

branches.question: What can you honestly count?

options.label: Push self-reporting
options.cost: Low coverage, high annoyance, and the people who log are not the people doing the most.

options.label: Count only what leaves a trace
options.cost: Undercounts by a lot, and is honest about it.

options.label: Stop counting
options.cost: No number, no grant, no argument.

well.label: A smaller true number
well.conditions: A trace-based measure is adopted.
well.chronicle: They counted what they could count and said so, and that turned out to be enough for half of it.

badly.label: A number that is wrong
badly.conditions: Self-reporting is pushed and the resulting figure is used.
changes: funding based on a biased sample
badly.chronicle: The number they used was mostly one person's hours and everybody knew it.

quietly.label: The sheet came down
quietly.chronicle: The sheet came down in March and nobody mentioned it.

seeds.source: data/events.json note that neither Point Lookout Bushcare nor Friends of Stradbroke Island publishes a working bee calendar, and that the monthly Saturday pattern in that pack is an invented modelling default; src/systems/manifest.js, which reserves src/systems/economy/chour.js for a community contribution ledger.
seeds.notes: This seed exists to keep the simulation honest about its own community contribution ledger. The blocker on counting community hours here is cultural, not regulatory: people do not self-report. A ledger that records money and traces rather than self-reported hours is the deliberate design, and this seed teaches the player why rather than modelling a fantasy of full participation.

seeds.title: A koala in the back tree
seeds.one_line: A young male turns up in a backyard at Point Lookout in October, and the dog next door is a lovely dog.
seeds.of_this_place: Koala breeding and dispersal peaks in spring and that is when young animals end up in township trees. Dog attack is the third recorded cause of koala death on this island. Nobody in this story has done anything wrong yet.

cast.why: Has never seen one in a tree before and is beside themselves about it.
Owns the lovely dog, has owned dogs here for thirty years, and is about to be asked to change something.
Gets the call, and the advice is almost always to leave it alone, which nobody wants to hear.
Checks the tree four times a day.
Would like the corridor trees on that block kept, and has no power to require it.

beats.name: October
beats.what_happens: Spring. Young animals moving. Someone hears one at night and does not know what it is.
beats.legible: The koala layer shows increased movement between habitat and township trees.
beats.chronicle: Something made a noise in the tree at the back about two in the morning.

beats.name: In the tree at the back
beats.what_happens: A young male in a backyard eucalypt. Fences on three sides. Dogs in two of the four adjoining yards. It has to come down and cross something to leave.
beats.legible: A koala agent in a township tree with a visible risk halo from adjacent dogs and roads.
beats.chronicle: It was in the gum at the back of number nine with dogs in two of the yards around it.

beats.name: Ask the neighbours
