beats.what_happens: The choice is not about the koala, it is about asking two households to keep their dogs in for a few nights. That is a small ask and it is also being told what to do in your own yard.
beats.legible: Two households show a compliance probability driven by their existing relationship values.
beats.chronicle: Somebody went and asked the neighbours to keep the dogs in for a few nights.

beats.name: Three nights
beats.what_happens: It stays three nights and goes. Or it does not. The difference is almost entirely whether the person asking had enough standing to be listened to.

sets.condition: if it is refused and the asker is a newcomer

beats.legible: The outcome is visibly driven by the relationship values, which the player can inspect.
beats.chronicle: They kept the dogs in for three nights and on the fourth morning it was gone.

beats.name: The tree
beats.what_happens: The following winter somebody applies to take the tree down because of the leaves in the gutter. That application is a different thread and this one is why it matters.
beats.legible: The tree is now flagged in the world as a corridor tree, and a later civic thread can reference it.
beats.chronicle: The next winter there was an application to take the tree out.

branches.question: Who asks, and do they have the standing?

options.label: A long-term neighbour asks
options.cost: Nothing much. It works.

options.label: The newcomer asks
options.cost: Reads as being told what to do.

options.label: Council contacts the households
options.cost: Guaranteed compliance and guaranteed resentment.

options.label: Nobody asks
options.cost: Nothing happens, most of the time.
effects: risk resolved by the ecology system, not by this seed

well.label: Gone by Thursday
well.conditions: The animal leaves the township unharmed.
well.chronicle: It was gone by Thursday and the kid was disappointed.

badly.label: The other outcome
badly.conditions: A dog attack or road strike occurs.
badly.chronicle: It did not get out of the yard and the two households have not spoken since.

quietly.label: Nobody ever knew
quietly.conditions: Default. It leaves overnight and only one person ever saw it.
quietly.chronicle: It went overnight and only one person ever saw it.

seeds.source: data/ecology.json seasonal_calendar spring entry, koala breeding and dispersal with a road strike and dog attack peak; sp-koala recorded mortality causes, dog attack 16 for 1997 to 2010; data/civic.json koala-habitat-overlay and dog-control-enforcement levers.
seeds.notes: The island koala population is genetically distinct after roughly 8,000 years of isolation, and disease is present but at lower clinical rates than stressed mainland populations. The simulation must not describe these animals as disease free. No population figure is stated anywhere in this seed.

seeds.title: The crew wants the Gorge
seeds.one_line: A small film crew wants to shoot at the headland at first light on a public holiday weekend, and every part of that sentence is a problem.
seeds.of_this_place: People make films here. The headland at dawn is the shot everybody wants, it is also a public walk with four hundred people a day on it, a car park with no spare bays, and Country with its own permissions that are not a production company's to grant themselves.

cast.why: Producing. Has done everything by the book on the mainland and has not done this here before.
Handles the permit and knows which three things this application has not thought about.
Parks in the spot the unit truck wants, every morning, for twenty years.
Gets three days of paid work out of it, which is a real thing on this island in winter.
Is watching where the tripods go on the dune.

beats.name: The shot
beats.what_happens: A small crew scouts the headland. The light is exactly what they came for and the walk is already full at six in the morning.
beats.legible: The headland crowd is high even at dawn, which the player can verify.
beats.chronicle: They scouted it at six and there were already forty people on the walk.

beats.name: Three things they did not think about
beats.what_happens: Parking for a unit truck where there are no spare bays. A crowd they cannot hold. And a set of permissions on Country that are not council's to give and are not theirs to assume.
beats.legible: Three separate constraint markers appear on the permit: parking, public access, and a cultural clearance step that the simulation shows as required and does not resolve.
beats.chronicle: The parking was the easiest of the three problems.

beats.name: Adapt or go somewhere else
beats.what_happens: Shoot a different location with a worse view and no constraints, shoot midweek in winter when the island wants the trade, or push for the weekend and wear everything.
beats.legible: Three schedules with a parking load, a crowd conflict and a local spend attached.
beats.chronicle: They moved it to a Tuesday in July.

beats.name: Who gets paid
beats.what_happens: A production that shoots midweek in winter spends money in a month when nothing else does. A production that shoots on a long weekend takes bays, blocks a walk and leaves nothing behind but a grievance.
beats.legible: Local spend and parking pressure move in opposite directions depending on the choice.
beats.chronicle: They spent about eleven thousand on the island in a week in July, which nobody else does.

beats.name: The footage
beats.what_happens: Something gets made. Whether it shows the island as a place people live or as scenery is decided in an edit suite somewhere else, and the island finds out when everybody else does.
beats.legible: A visitor demand modifier that arrives months later with no warning, which is exactly how this works.
beats.chronicle: It came out in March and the car park was full for a month.

branches.question: Whose weekend is it?

options.label: Midweek in the off season
options.cost: Worse weather, better everything else.
effects: local spend in a dead month

options.label: The long weekend they wanted
options.cost: Bays, the walk, and about forty people's morning.

options.label: They shoot somewhere else
options.cost: Nothing gained and nothing lost.

well.label: A week in July
well.conditions: The shoot happens off peak with local crew engaged.
well.chronicle: They shot it in July, hired four locals and left.

badly.label: A unit truck in the car park
badly.conditions: The shoot happens in peak.
changes: a durable grievance about film crews
badly.chronicle: The unit truck took six bays on the Saturday of the long weekend and nobody forgot it.

quietly.label: They went to the mainland
quietly.chronicle: They shot it somewhere on the mainland in the end.

seeds.source: General knowledge of location filming logistics, applied to data/places.json north-gorge-walk and data/transport.json parking, which records no published bay count for any car park at Point Lookout.
seeds.notes: The cultural clearance step in beat two is rendered as a required constraint and is never resolved, granted, refused or described by this pack. Any depiction of a permission process on Country is out of scope and belongs in docs/CULTURAL-REVIEW.md. No filming permit process for this island was verified and none is described in detail. No festival, production company or funding body is named.

seeds.title: An old shift
seeds.one_line: Somebody who worked the mine for twenty two years walks through the rehabilitation area on a Sunday and does not say much about it.
seeds.of_this_place: Sand mining ended here and the ground it left is being rehabilitated. That is unambiguously good for the island and it was also several hundred people's jobs, some of them held by families who have been here for generations. Both of those are true and the second one is rarely said out loud.

cast.why: Twenty two years, a good wage, a house paid off, and a set of skills the island no longer buys.
Their kid, who works in rehabilitation or tourism, and earns about sixty per cent of what their parent did.
Works the same ground for a different purpose and gets on with the ex-mine worker better than either expected.
Says something well meant about the mine closing and does not understand the silence that follows.
Was against the mine the whole time and went to the same funerals.

beats.name: Sunday
beats.what_happens: An ordinary Sunday. A walk on ground that used to be a work site and is now scrub coming back.
beats.legible: The rehabilitation areas render with a visible vegetation recovery state.
beats.chronicle: The wattle was coming up thick where the haul road used to be.

beats.name: It looks like nothing was ever there
beats.what_happens: The rehabilitation is working. Somewhere under it is a shift roster, a smoko shed and about four hundred people's twenties.
beats.legible: A rehabilitation progress metric hits a milestone, which the ecology panel reports as a straightforward good.
beats.chronicle: You could not tell what had been there, which was the point of it.

beats.name: What replaces a wage
beats.what_happens: The island has tourism, rehabilitation work, ranger positions and construction. None of them pay what the mine did and most of them stop in winter. The question is whether the simulation is honest about that.
beats.legible: A wage comparison across the island's occupations, with seasonality shown.
beats.chronicle: The jobs that replaced it paid less and stopped in March.

beats.name: The kid works two jobs
beats.what_happens: The next generation holds two seasonal jobs to make one income. The house is paid off and cannot be extended. Nobody frames this as a loss because the mine closing was the right thing.
beats.legible: Household income composition shows multiple seasonal jobs where one full time job used to be.
beats.chronicle: She had two jobs and between them they were not one job.

beats.name: Nothing said
beats.what_happens: They walk back to the car. Nothing gets said about any of it. That is the coda and it is deliberate.
beats.legible: No metric changes. One chronicle line.
beats.chronicle: They walked back to the car and did not talk about it.

branches.question: What does the island do about year-round work?

options.label: Fund rehabilitation and ranger positions properly
options.cost: A recurrent budget line, which is the hardest kind.

options.label: Grow the visitor economy
options.cost: More seasonal jobs, more pressure on everything else.

options.label: Nothing
options.cost: The next generation leaves.

well.label: A job that does not stop
well.conditions: Year-round employment rises within the window.
well.chronicle: The ranger position went permanent and that was worth more than it looked.

badly.label: Two jobs and neither
badly.conditions: Seasonal work only.
badly.chronicle: She took a job at Cleveland in the end and drove the boat both ways.

quietly.label: Nothing said
quietly.chronicle: They walked back to the car.

seeds.source: data/civic.json post-mining issue; data/geography.json rehabilitation_areas; data/residents.json household archetype ex-mine-worker-couple-dunwich and occupation mine-rehabilitation-worker.
seeds.notes: No mine employment figure, closure date detail, wage comparison or rehabilitation completion schedule is stated, because none was verified in this pass. The four hundred people in beat two is a character's impression, not a figure, and the director should render the simulation's own historical employment number or omit the clause. This seed must not be written as an argument for or against the mine.

seeds.title: What it costs to get home
seeds.one_line: A fare change lands, and a household that crosses twice a week does the sum on the back of an envelope and does not like the answer.
seeds.of_this_place: The vehicle ferry uses airline-style dynamic pricing on a route that some people use as a driveway. A resident flat fare exists and has an end date. For a household that crosses for work, school, specialists or a funeral, the crossing is not a ticket, it is a standing cost of living here.

cast.why: Crosses for work. The fare is a line item in a household budget that has no slack in it.
Crosses for appointments that are not optional and cannot be scheduled around a fare.
Builds the crossing into every quote, which is why everything on this island costs more.
Crosses about twelve times a year and genuinely had not noticed.
Has no lever on a fare set by an operator and gets the complaints anyway.

beats.name: The standing cost
beats.what_happens: A household crossing twice a week, every week, for years. It is not a trip, it is a commute with a ticket price.
beats.legible: A recurring household cost line for crossings, visible in the economy panel.
beats.chronicle: They crossed twice a week and had done for eleven years.

beats.name: The sum
beats.what_happens: The fare structure changes, or the resident concession approaches its end date, and somebody works out the annual number for the first time.
beats.legible: An annual crossing cost figure appears for the household, computed by the sim.
beats.chronicle: The annual figure was more than the rates and the insurance put together.

beats.name: Cross less, or cross differently
beats.what_happens: Leave the car on the mainland and walk on, which means a long term car park with a waitlist measured in years. Cross less, which means missing things. Or absorb it, which means something else in the budget goes.
beats.legible: Three costs, one of which is a waitlist the household cannot join in time.
beats.chronicle: The long term car park had a waitlist measured in years.

beats.name: What gets dropped
beats.what_happens: Something goes. A specialist appointment moves to a phone call. A kid stops doing the sport on the mainland. Somebody stops going to see their mother every fortnight.
beats.legible: A specific recurring need stops being met, and the player can see which.
beats.chronicle: The fortnightly trip to see his mother became a monthly one.

beats.name: Everybody has this sum
beats.what_happens: It turns out at the club that four other households have done the same arithmetic and nobody had mentioned it. That is either the start of something or it is not.
beats.legible: The ferry cost burden metric becomes a visible civic pressure with a named constituency.
beats.chronicle: Four other people at the club had done the same sum and none of them had said anything either.

branches.question: Is there anything the island can do about a fare it does not set?

options.label: Advocate for a resident fare arrangement
options.cost: Slow, and it depends on a government and an operator.

options.label: Push for more long term parking on the mainland side
options.cost: Land at Toondah, which is its own fight.

options.label: Nothing
options.cost: Households absorb it until they cannot.

well.label: A resident arrangement holds
well.conditions: A concession or priority arrangement is retained or extended.
well.chronicle: The resident fare was extended and about four hundred households exhaled.

badly.label: Something gets dropped
badly.conditions: No change and an unmet need persists past 90 days.
changes: a household becomes a leaver candidate
badly.chronicle: The trips got fewer and then they stopped.

quietly.label: They absorbed it
quietly.chronicle: They absorbed it and stopped going out.

seeds.source: data/transport.json fares section: the vehicle ferry uses airline-style dynamic pricing, a resident flat fare of A$59 for a standard car with a A$69 variant and a A$20 public holiday and peak Christmas surcharge, with conflicting reported end dates of 31 March 2026 and 31 March 2027; the SeaLink long term car park at Toondah with a waitlist reported as years rather than months; data/civic.json cost-of-crossing issue.
seeds.notes: Every SeaLink page returns HTTP 403 to an automated fetch, so no fare in this repo was read from the operator. The Stradbroke Flyer fare is completely unknown and is recorded as null in the transport pack. This seed therefore never displays a fare. It displays the simulation's own crossing cost index and the household's own annual total.

seeds.title: Between the flags
seeds.one_line: Somebody gets into trouble at a beach the patrol does not cover, and the people who go in are the ones who happen to be there.
seeds.of_this_place: Point Lookout Surf Life Saving Club describes itself as the only surf life saving club in Australia to actively patrol two beaches and rove six others. That is a real operational fact and it is also a sentence about how much coastline a volunteer club is covering.

also_requires.note: A run-out tide feeding a rip.

cast.why: Off duty, at a different beach, with a board on the car because they always have a board on the car.
Picked the beach because it was empty, which is the exact wrong reason.
Fishing off the rocks nearby and is the first person to see it.
Grew up here, swims like it, and is fifteen.
Twenty five minutes away on a road with a bus on it.

beats.name: The empty beach
beats.what_happens: A hot day. The patrolled beaches are packed. A family drives to one that is not, because there is room.
beats.legible: Crowd distribution across beaches with the patrol coverage drawn on.
beats.chronicle: Cylinder was packed so they drove around to one that was not.

beats.name: The gutter
beats.what_happens: A run-out tide and a bank set up a rip. Somebody is thirty metres further out than they meant to be and cannot get back.
beats.legible: A rip renders on the water and an agent enters it.
beats.chronicle: The tide was running out over the bank and one of them got taken past where they could stand.

beats.name: Who goes in
beats.what_happens: The person who is qualified and off duty. The teenager who is not qualified and is the strongest swimmer there. Or nobody, and the call goes to the club and the ambulance.
beats.legible: Response options with a time and a risk, including the risk to the rescuer.
beats.chronicle: The one with the board went.

beats.name: It is over in four minutes
beats.what_happens: Most of these are over quickly and are not dramatic. What is left is a family sitting on the sand, a volunteer who has to go back to their own day, and a fifteen year old who now knows something about themselves.
beats.legible: The incident resolves, and volunteer fatigue and standing both rise.
beats.chronicle: It took about four minutes and then everybody sat on the sand for a while.

beats.name: Nippers
beats.what_happens: The family joins the club for the season, or they never come back. Both happen about equally often and neither is a moral.
beats.legible: Club membership either rises by one household or does not.
beats.chronicle: They put the kids in Nippers the next season.

branches.question: Who goes in?

options.label: The off duty lifesaver
options.cost: Their day, and the club's exposure.

options.label: The teenager
options.cost: It works, and it should not have been their job.
effects: a fifteen year old carrying something
a conversation at the club afterwards

options.label: Nobody goes in and the call is made
options.cost: Twenty five minutes on a road with a bus on it.
effects: outcome determined by the health system, not this seed

well.label: Out and sitting on the sand
well.conditions: Resolution within ten minutes with no injury.
well.chronicle: They were out inside five minutes and the club got two new Nippers out of it.

badly.label: A long response
badly.conditions: No one is able to respond before help arrives.
badly.chronicle: It took twenty five minutes for anybody official to get there.

quietly.label: They got themselves out
quietly.conditions: Default. The rip pushes them onto the bank and they walk in.
quietly.chronicle: It let them go onto the bank and they walked in, which is what usually happens.

seeds.source: Point Lookout Surf Life Saving Club's own description: the only surf life saving club in Australia to actively patrol two beaches, Main and Cylinder, and to provide roving water and land patrols of six other beaches on North Stradbroke Island; the club was founded in 1947 (https://pointlookoutslsc2.wordpress.com/about-the-club/, and https://stradbrokeisland.com/point-lookout-surf-life/); data/events.json surf-patrol-season period and nippers event; data/places.json beach records.
seeds.notes: This seed must never describe an injury, a resuscitation or a death. The three endings are resolution, self-resolution, and a slow response whose outcome is left to the health system. Current patrol seasons and hours for the club were not confirmed against a live source and are flagged in the places pack.

seeds.title: After the rain
seeds.one_line: Two hundred millimetres in three days, and the question at the seafood festival is whether the water is clean.
seeds.of_this_place: The island grows and eats Sydney rock oysters and runs a seafood festival. It also has wastewater infrastructure sized for a resident population, and heavy rain is when the two facts meet.

cast.why: Has a monitoring result and a decision about whether to say anything before a public event.
Has ordered seafood for an event that is on Saturday whatever happens.
Has been asking about the outfall and the overflows for eleven years.
Will not eat anything out of that end of the bay after rain and never has.
Bought a ticket and would like to know, and is entitled to.

beats.name: Three days of it
beats.what_happens: A trough sits over the bay and it rains for three days. The lakes come up, the tracks wash, and every drain on the island runs.
beats.legible: Rainfall accumulation and lake levels both visibly rise.
beats.chronicle: It rained for three days and the tracks all washed out.

beats.name: The result
beats.what_happens: Nearshore water quality drops. Whether that is stormwater, the wastewater system, or both is exactly the argument, and it takes days to know.
beats.legible: A nearshore water quality metric drops with a lag, and the cause is ambiguous in the UI on purpose.
beats.chronicle: The nearshore results came back poor and nobody could say which part of it was the sewage.

beats.name: Say it now or wait for the test
beats.what_happens: Announce a precaution before the event on incomplete information, or wait two days for a result that will land after the festival.
beats.legible: A timing decision with a public health cost on one side and an economic cost on the other, both quantified.
beats.chronicle: They put the advisory out on the Thursday.

beats.name: Either way somebody is angry
beats.what_happens: Announce early and the event takes a hit and the operators wear it. Wait and the trust cost is much larger and lasts much longer, particularly if the result is bad.
beats.legible: Two different metric paths depending on the choice, with the trust path recovering much more slowly.
beats.chronicle: The festival was down about a third and half the town thought that was the wrong call.

beats.name: The outfall question
beats.what_happens: Somebody asks the wastewater capacity question again, properly, in public, with a number attached this time. It goes into a budget process and comes out in about four years.
beats.legible: The wastewater capacity metric becomes a tracked civic pressure with a constituency behind it.
beats.chronicle: The question about capacity went into a budget process and will come out in about four years.

branches.question: Precaution or certainty?

options.label: Announce a precaution
options.cost: An event takes a third off its gate and the operators pay for it.

options.label: Wait for the result
options.cost: If it is bad, the trust cost is very large and very slow to recover.
effects: consultation_trust -0.15 if the result is poor

options.label: Publish the data without an advisory
options.cost: Honest, and it puts the decision on people who do not have time to read it.

well.label: Told people early
well.conditions: An advisory is issued before the event.
well.chronicle: They said it on the Thursday and took the hit.

badly.label: Waited
badly.conditions: No advisory and the result is poor.
badly.chronicle: The result came out on the Tuesday and it had been poor the whole weekend.

quietly.label: It came back fine
quietly.conditions: Default. The result is acceptable and nobody hears about any of it.
quietly.chronicle: It came back fine and nobody ever knew there had been a question.

seeds.source: data/civic.json water-and-wastewater issue with the water_quality_nearshore and wastewater_capacity metrics; data/ecology.json sp-sydney-rock-oyster; data/events.json straddie-oyster-and-seafood-festival.
seeds.notes: Marked low. No wastewater treatment arrangement, outfall location, overflow history or water quality monitoring programme for this island was verified in this pass, and none is described. The seed asserts only that heavy rain and nearshore water quality are linked, which is general, and lets the simulation supply every number. If the infrastructure pack establishes the real arrangement, rewrite of_this_place and the beats before this seed is used.
